papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is standard of care for inoperable stage I or II non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). KEYNOTE-867 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03924869) evaluated the addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT in participants diagnosed with stage I or II NSCLC that was inoperable or in participants who refused surgery. METHODS: Adults with untreated, stage I or II (T1 to limited T3, N0, M0) NSCLC (AJCC 8th edition) that was inoperable, or adults who refused surgery, were randomly assigned 1:1 to thoracic SBRT to primary tumors for ≤2 weeks concomitantly with pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo once every 3 weeks for ≤17 cycles. The primary end point was event-free survival (EFS) by blinded independent central review. RESULTS: A total of 448 participants were randomly assigned to SBRT plus pembrolizumab (n = 227) or SBRT plus placebo (n = 221). The median time from random assignment to the data cutoff date (June 11, 2024) for the prespecified first interim analysis was 20.6 (range, 1.3-56.8) months. The median EFS (95% CI) was 31.2 (22.5 to 39.1) months and 28.3 (19.8 to 33.1) months for the pembrolizumab and placebo arms, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.69 to 1.24]; P = .2932). Among participants who received ≥1 dose of study treatment, grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 46/226 (20.4%) participants in the pembrolizumab arm and 8/218 (3.7%) participants in the placebo arm. There were five treatment-related deaths all of which occurred in the pembrolizumab arm (2.2%). CONCLUSION: The addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT did not improve EFS and was associated with a higher incidence of treatment-related AEs compared with SBRT alone in participants with inoperable stage I or II NSCLC. Based on the benefit-risk profile, the KEYNOTE-867 trial was prematurely stopped, and all study treatment was discontinued.

papers.title_en: Venous Thromboembolism Reporting in Fusion-Positive NSCLC Treated with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Systematic Review of Safety Reporting and Protocol-Level Provisions in Phase I-IV Clinical Trials.
papers.authors: Citarella F, Fiorenti M, Fragale C, Sini C, Passiglia F, Cortellini A, Bronte G
papers.affiliation_highlight: Thoracic Department, Division of Thoracic Medical Oncology, Istituto Nazionale Tumori "Fondazione G.
papers.results: 共审查61项研究条目（58项唯一试验）的108份报告来源；PE与DVT为主要报告事件；14项研究条目仅通过全文发表报告事件，19项仅通过在线试验更新报告，15项通过两种来源报告；超过40%的研究条目缺乏方案层面的抗凝治疗条款，近60%缺乏VTE相关入排限制；事件定义、报告实践、安全性判定与观察期存在明显异质性
papers.authors_conclusion: 在融合阳性NSCLC试验中，事件判定与报告方式的异质性——而非血栓栓塞事件的真实稀缺——是现有证据的主要局限；提高安全性报告标准化并整合注册平台与发表数据，可改善未来研究的完整性、可比性与可解释性
papers.ai_note: 本研究未汇总VTE发生率，无法区分“报告不足”与“事件本身少见”，作者“异质性而非真实稀缺”的结论属推断而非本研究实测；仅描述报告条目的计数，未按试验规模/暴露人时加权，亦未评估各来源间一致性（如kappa）；“>40%”“近60%”为文字性比例，无置信区间与统计检验；检索策略、筛选流程、偏倚评估工具及是否预设方案（PROSPERO）在摘要中均信息不足。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria. RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods. CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Physical deterioration and disease progression during neoadjuvant treatment can preclude tumor surgery in patients with gastroesophageal cancer. Whether preoperative exercise training can increase the probability of undergoing tumor surgery remains unknown. OBJECTIVE: To compare exercise training with usual care on the likelihood of not undergoing tumor surgery with curative intent after neoadjuvant treatment for gastroesophageal cancer. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: PRESET-RCT was a single-blinded, parallel-group, 2-arm, superiority randomized clinical trial. Patients with gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma scheduled to undergo treatment with curative intent, including neoadjuvant treatment, and with no contraindication to exercise training were eligible. Participants were enrolled at University Hospital Copenhagen, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark, from August 16, 2018, to September 23, 2022, with final follow-up on October 22, 2024. Data analysis was performed from March 2023 to May 2025. INTERVENTION: The participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative exercise training from diagnosis until tumor surgery or control. The intervention consisted of twice-weekly concurrent aerobic exercise and resistance training. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was not undergoing tumor surgery with curative intent. The secondary outcomes were treatment tolerance and overall survival. RESULTS: In total, 207 participants (73.7%) were randomized and 202 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analyses (mean [SD] age, 65.3 [8.5] years; 161 [78.9%] male; 170 [83.3%] with gastroesophageal junction cancer), with 101 randomized to each group. In the exercise group, 10 (9.9%) did not undergo tumor surgery with curative intent compared with 8 (7.9%) in the control group (odds ratio, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.48-3.38; P = .62). There were no between-group differences in permanent discontinuation of neoadjuvant treatment (odds ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.38-1.72) or postoperative complications (odds ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.61-2.20). The overall survival rates at 3 years for the exercise and control group were 51.0% and 65.0%, respectively (hazard ratio, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.02-2.45). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, preoperative exercise training did not increase the likelihood of undergoing tumor surgery for patients with gastroesophageal cancer. The findings do not support the use of exercise training during neoadjuvant treatment to improve surgical outcomes, and further research is needed to determine its effects on long-term outcomes. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03490565.

papers.abstract_en: Confinement architectures stabilise active metal nanoparticles while preserving molecular accessibility, which proves crucial for heterogeneous catalysis. However, existing methods for preparing encapsulated catalysts such as mesoporous oxides, zeolites, and metal-organic frameworks are costly, complex, and often unreliable. Solid‑state reactions offer a promising alternative, yet conventional pathways yield thermodynamically stable phases that limit activity. Here, we propose a facile, template-free strategy that intercepts amorphous intermediates during solid‑state reactions to form encapsulation layers for active metals. We select ammonia decomposition reaction (ADR, 2NH3 → N2 + 3H2) as the target catalytic reaction, which is a pivotal route to COx‑free hydrogen and affords the high‑temperature, reducing environment that drives solid‑state transformations. During ADR conditions, commercial BaCO3 and Al2O3 act as solid‑state reactants, forming Al2O3-BaO encapsulation layers around Co or Ni nanoparticles. The layers effectively restrict nanoparticle growth. Amorphous Al2O3 facilitates NH3 adsorption, and amorphous BaO accelerates N2/H2 release and enables N-H activation. As a result, the encapsulated catalyst delivers an intrinsic rate of 1,358 mmol H2·gmetal-1·min-1 that surpasses existing non‑noble metal catalysts, alongside excellent durability during 480 h. This approach offers a blueprint for constructing durable confinement architectures in encapsulated metal catalysts.

papers.abstract_en: Metabolic reprogramming, the fundamental process by which cells adapt to fluctuations in energy demands, is pivotal in the pathophysiology of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases (CCVDs). Aberrant reprogramming of glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism is intricately associated with pathological processes in CCVDs such as cardiac hypertrophy, atherosclerosis, and ischemia-reperfusion injury. This metabolic remodeling disrupts the dynamic balance of metabolites (cc, acetyl-CoA and lactate) in the cardio-cerebrovascular systems, thereby inducing abnormal post-translational modifications (PTMs) on histones and non-histone proteins. These PTMs drive disease progression by modulating gene transcription or the activity of key proteins, which subsequently influences downstream signaling pathways. Here, we systematically examine the regulatory enzymes and functional roles of nine recently characterized acylation modifications: crotonylation, β-hydroxybutyrylation, 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation, succinylation, malonylation, glutarylation, lactylation, propionylation, and butyrylation. Furthermore, this review elaborates on the molecular mechanisms, crosstalk and the latest preclinical advancements regarding these acylations in CCVDs, emphasizing the influence of distinct acylation patterns on various pathological processes and highlighting the clinical translational prospects of targeting these novel modifications for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: In clinical trials, the messenger RNA (mRNA)-1345 vaccine provided protection against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) illness. Data on mRNA-1345 effectiveness in broader patient populations are needed. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effectiveness of mRNA-1345 vaccination during a single respiratory illness season. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used a target trial emulation framework to assess veterans 50 years and older receiving care in the Veterans Health Administration. Eligible vaccine recipients were matched with up to 4 unvaccinated individuals in 4 monthly, nested, sequential trials from October 1, 2025, to January 31, 2026. Outcomes were ascertained through May 31, 2026, or 24 weeks. EXPOSURE: A single dose of mRNA-1345 RSV vaccine vs no RSV vaccination. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was any positive RSV test result from day 14 after the matched index date. Secondary outcomes included RSV-associated emergency department (ED) or urgent care (UC) encounters and RSV-associated hospitalizations. Vaccine effectiveness was estimated as 100 × (1 - risk ratio). A sensitivity analysis comparing veterans who received same-day mRNA-1345 and influenza vaccination to influenza vaccination alone (active comparator arm) was performed to explore potential bias from differences in health care-seeking behavior and outcome ascertainment between comparator groups. RESULTS: A total of 74 926 vaccinated veterans were matched to 286 425 unique control individuals, weighted to represent 74 926 individuals, for a total of 149 852 study participants (median [IQR] age, 73.0 [63.3-78.6] years; 136 756 [91.3%] male). During a median (IQR) follow-up of 160 (130-168) days, estimated vaccine effectiveness was 60.3% (95% CI, 49.0%-70.4%) against any documented infection, 60.2% (95% CI, 47.2%-71.5%) against RSV-associated ED or UC encounters, and 81.8% (95% CI, 58.1%-99.9%) against RSV-associated hospitalizations. Estimated effectiveness against documented infections decreased with increasing age, from 82.9% (95% CI, 64.0%-96.7%) in the 50- to 59-year age group to 28.6% (95% CI, -12.0% to 60.4%) in the 80-year or older age group. With an active comparator arm, estimated effectiveness was 67.1% (95% CI, 48.9%-82.6%) against documented RSV infections, 69.5% (95% CI, 49.7%-85.4%) against RSV-associated ED and UC encounters, and 86.9% (95% CI, 56.5%-100.0%) against RSV-associated hospitalizations. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study using a target trial emulation of mRNA-1345 vaccine effectiveness during 24 weeks, vaccination was associated with protection against RSV illness and associated health care use in adults 50 years and older. Comparative effectiveness studies are needed to determine the relative benefits of available RSV vaccine products.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Recurrent pulmonary exacerbations contribute substantially to lung function decline in people with cystic fibrosis (CF). Inhalation therapies are a cornerstone of standard of care, yet adherence to inhalation therapies is variable and data on the relationship between adherence and pulmonary exacerbations remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To assess the impact of multimodal telemonitoring and coaching on adherence and pulmonary exacerbations in people with CF. METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter, unblinded, randomized, controlled trial people with CF aged ≥12 years were randomized (1:1) to either standard of care or an intervention involving continuous objective home monitoring of inhalation adherence, weekly home spirometry, a self-management app, professional telephone coaching, and optional video conferencing over 18 months. The primary endpoint was time to first pulmonary exacerbation. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: 296 participants were included with a mean age of 31.3 (SD 10.8) years, 54.1% females, mean FEV1% predicted of 70.2% (SD 24.7), 52.7% chronically infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and 85.1% on triple CFTR modulator therapy. Baseline adherence was higher in the intervention group (58.1%) than in the control group (44.0%) and remained higher throughout the study (last 6 months: 49.2% vs. 32.6%). Time to first exacerbation did not differ between groups. However, across all participants, a 10% increase in adherence correlated with a 9% reduction in pulmonary exacerbation risk. Participants with FEV1<40% had a 2.4-fold higher risk of exacerbations. CONCLUSION: Multimodal telemedicine improved inhalation therapy adherence. The association between higher adherence and reduced exacerbations highlights the ongoing importance of inhalation therapy in CF, even with widespread CFTR modulator use. Clinical trial registered with German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00024642).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Constipation is common in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD), and individual responses to non-pharmacological interventions may vary substantially. This exploratory study investigated whether baseline gut microbiota characteristics were associated with short-term response to acupressure combined with thermal stimulation in MHD patients with functional constipation. METHODS: This responder analysis was based on a randomized two-sequence crossover study. Clinical data and fecal samples obtained immediately before each participant entered the 14-day intervention period were analyzed. Participants with an increase of ≥1 bowel movement (BM) per week were classified as responders (R), and those with <1 BM/week as non-responders (NR). Baseline gut microbiota were characterized using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and genus-level differential abundance were evaluated. ANCOM-BC2 was performed with adjustment for baseline BM/week, sex, and diabetes mellitus, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction and pseudocount sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Twenty-six participants were included, of whom 9 (34.6%) met the predefined response criterion. Alpha-diversity did not differ significantly between R and NR groups, and beta-diversity showed no overall community separation (ANOSIM R=-0.044, P = 0.6751). Lactonifactor was nominally higher in responders in the unadjusted analysis (P = 0.015) but was not significant after multiple-testing correction (FDR = 0.86). In adjusted ANCOM-BC2 analysis, Veillonella (β=5.319, FDR = 0.0347) and Lactobacillus (β=3.621, FDR = 0.0459) were associated with responder status; however, neither association was robust to pseudocount sensitivity analysis. PICRUSt2 identified no significant between-group differences in predicted functional pathways. CONCLUSION: Baseline microbial diversity and community structure were similar between responders and non-responders. Veillonella and Lactobacillus showed adjusted associations with response, but neither was robust in sensitivity analysis. These findings should therefore be regarded as exploratory rather than predictive. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to validate these findings and determine their clinical relevance.

papers.abstract_en: T cell correlates of COVID-19 risk are poorly defined, particularly in people with HIV (PWH). CoVPN 3008 ( NCT05168813 ) Part A was a prospective 14,002-participant cohort study that administered one or two doses of mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine, depending on baseline SARS-CoV-2 serostatus, in participants (83% PWH) in sub-Saharan Africa. Participants self-monitored for prespecified COVID-19 symptoms, defined by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention symptom criteria. Previous work showed that protection from COVID-19 was superior for hybrid versus vaccine-induced immunity, and that neutralizing antibody titers inversely associated with COVID-19 risk. In the present work, we measured T cell responses to Spike and Nucleocapsid at baseline and 4 weeks post last-vaccination (Peak) in a case-cohort study and assessed them as correlates of risk. In Hybrid Group PWH (n = 22 cases), COVID-19 risk over 6 months decreased with increasing Peak Spike BA.4/5-specific CD4 + T cell responses, from 15.8%, 4.7%, and 0% risk at 0.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% IFN-γ and/or IL-2 response magnitude, respectively. Including baseline Spike-specific neutralizing antibody titer and Peak CD4 + T cell functionality score in the same model increased the association's strength (overall p < 0.001). Thus, CD4 + T cell responses are an independent correlate of COVID-19 risk among PWH with pre-existing SARS-CoV-2 immunity.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Sepsis-associated lung injury (SALI) is a lethal infection-induced complication with high mortality and limited targeted therapies. Dysregulated lactate metabolism is closely linked to SALI, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the role and molecular mechanism of EZH2 (Enhancer of zeste homolog 2) lactylation in SALI development, thereby uncovering a novel exploitable therapeutic target. METHODS: A total of 209 ICU patients were enrolled and divided into the SALI group (n = 104) and non-SALI group (n = 105) to detect serum lactate levels. Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mouse models and endothelial cell-specific Ezh2 knockout (Ezh2ECKO) mouse models were established. Combined with lactate and lactate dehydrogenase inhibitor intervention, multi-omics analysis, ChIP, qPCR, immunofluorescence and other techniques were used in the study. RESULTS: Serum lactate levels were significantly elevated in patients with SALI and model mice, and lung tissue lactate levels were elevated in model mice. Lactate levels were positively associated with inflammatory markers and lung injury severity. EZH2 underwent site-specific lactylation at lysine 30 and 406 (EZH2 K30/K406la) in SALI, which was enhanced with disease progression. Inhibiting lactate production or EZH2 lactylation improved pulmonary function, reduced inflammatory infiltration and pathological lung tissue damage. EZH2 K30/K406la downregulated CITED2 (CBP-p300 interacting transactivator with Glu/Asp-rich carboxy-terminal domain 2) expression by reducing its occupancy at the CITED2 promoter and altering CITED2 promoter activity, relieving the inhibition of the NF-κB (Nuclear Factor-kappa B) pathway and exacerbating inflammatory responses and endothelial dysfunction. CONCLUSION: EZH2 lactylation aggravates SALI via the CITED2/NF-κB axis, highlighting this epigenetic modification as a promising therapeutic target that opens a new pharmacological avenue for developing site-specific inhibitors to combat SALI.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal cancer (EC) is highly lethal due to late diagnosis, and accurate non-invasive tools for early detection and subtyping remain lacking. Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) fragmentomics offers a promising biomarker source. In this large multi-center study enrolling 1,260 participants spanning healthy control (HC), benign esophageal diseases (BED), precancerous lesions and EC patients, we developed two machine learning models based on plasma ccf-mtDNA fragmentomic profiles: an EC detection (ED) model and a pathological subtyping prediction (PSP) model. The ED model achieved an AUC of 0.9706 (EC vs. non-EC) in the training cohort, with high performance in internal (0.9762), external (0.9748), and Chinese minority (0.9668, Uyghur and Kazakh) validation cohorts. At the optimal cut-off, it yielded 92.16% sensitivity for stage I EC in the combined validation cohort and correctly identified 93.10% of early EC cases missed by preoperative biopsy. It also discriminated high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia from non-EC with an AUC of 0.9597. The PSP model distinguished ESCC from EAC with 89.71% accuracy, improving to 90.74% after integrating key clinical parameters. In summary, ccf-mtDNA fragmentomics provides a robust, non-invasive platform for early EC detection, precancerous risk stratification, and histological subtyping, demonstrating strong potential to transform clinical management.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: With growing evidence and evolving guidelines, organ preservation with watch and wait for stage II to III rectal cancer after neoadjuvant therapy is increasingly implemented. However, the true frequency of watch-and-wait use is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To estimate rates of intentional organ preservation with watch and wait by evaluating secular trends across age groups. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the National Cancer Database (NCDB), with analyses conducted in September 2025. Patients with stage II to III rectal cancer diagnosed between 2006 and 2023 who received neoadjuvant chemoradiation in Commission on Cancer-accredited hospitals participating in the NCDB across the US were included. EXPOSURE: Age, year of diagnosis, and treatment strategy (proctectomy vs nonsurgical management). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome consisted of watch-and-wait rates, defined as excess nonsurgical management greater than baseline. To account for nonsurgical management unrelated to the decision for watch and wait, joinpoint regression estimated baseline rates of nonsurgical management and annual percentage changes. A secondary analysis examined associations of age and year with watch-and-wait rates using multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 101 001 patients with rectal cancer (median [IQR] age, 60 [51-69] years; 37 957 female [37.58%]), 84 324 underwent surgery and 16 677 did not. Baseline rates of nonsurgical management remained stable through 2014. Joinpoints occurred in 2014 and 2019, with annual percentage changes of -0.45% (95% CI, -2.26% to 0.78%; P = .42) in 2006 to 2014, 9.83% (95% CI, 4.66% to 13.73%; P = .001) in 2015 to 2018, and 21.71% (95% CI, 17.74% to 29.57%; P < .001) in 2019 to 2023. Baseline nonsurgical management increased with age, from 1331 of 19 785 patients younger than 50 years (6.73%) to 1748 of 6210 patients aged 80 years and older (28.15%). Earlier adoption occurred in older patients; the group aged 80 years and older surpassed 5-percentage point excess watch and wait by 2015 (33.78% annual rate vs 28.15% baseline rate [5.63-percentage point excess]) and 10% by 2017 (39.56% annual rate vs 28.15% baseline rate [11.41-percentage point excess]), compared with 2019 (12.88% annual rate vs 6.73% baseline rate [6.15-percentage point excess]) and 2021 (20.75% annual rate vs 6.73% baseline rate [14.02%] excess) in patients younger than 50 years. Overall, watch and wait increased from 140 of 6101 patients (2.30%) in 2015 to 2068 of 6280 patients (32.94%) in 2023. Increasing year (odds ratio for 2023 vs 2006, 6.23; 95% CI, 5.48 to 7.09) and older age (odds ratio for ages ≥80 vs <50 years, 4.25; 95% CI, 3.98 to 4.54) were independently associated with nonsurgical management (both P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, watch-and-wait rates increased across all age groups, with a marked acceleration after 2019 suggesting evidence-concordant adoption of the watch-and-wait approach. This underscores the need for careful patient selection, accurate clinical response assessment, and rigorous surveillance monitoring to ensure safe oncologic outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reactivation of human herpesviruses (HHVs), particularly EBV, is associated with more severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of Long COVID (LC). Reactivation of HHVs has been previously implicated in hormonal dysregulation, which has also been observed in LC, suggesting a potential link. This study aims to examine the relationship between LC symptoms and salivary HHV DNA, cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol levels. METHODS: Our cross-sectional, case-control study enrolled 45 participants with LC, and 45 age-sex-matched controls. Surveys and validated health questionnaires were used to collect demographics, medical history, and symptom profiles. Saliva was self-collected at waking, 15, 30, and 45 min, and 8 and 16 h after waking, across two consecutive days. Salivary cortisol, testosterone and oestradiol were measured, and extracted nucleic acid was tested for EBV, HSV 1/2, HCMV and HHV-6 A/B using multiplex qPCR, and for SARS-CoV-2 and RNaseP using RT-qPCR. FINDINGS: Detection of salivary EBV and HHV-6 DNA copies was highest early in the morning. There were no significant differences in salivary cortisol, testosterone, or oestradiol, or in EBV or HHV-6 DNA between the LC and control groups. However, salivary HHV-6 DNA levels were positively associated with a greater aggregated LC propensity score (r = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.02-0.44, p = 0.015, adj. p = 0.030), as well as anxiety (β = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.02-1.36, p = 0.045) and depression (β = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.05-0.42, p = 0.013) scores. INTERPRETATION: The observed correlation between salivary HHV-6 DNA and symptom severity suggests HHV-6 may contribute to post-acute disease, though mechanisms remain unclear. While we did not identify a relationship between salivary EBV DNA and LC, EBV may still play a role at earlier time points in the disease course, or in compartments not sampled in this study. These findings highlight the potential importance of HHV-6 in LC pathophysiology and underscore the need for longitudinal, multi-compartment studies of herpesvirus reactivation in LC. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Inguinal and femoral hernias in women show a reported diagnostic gap, with systematic evidence supported by cohorts composed of approximately 84% men. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a descriptive, retrospective, cross-sectional observational study at a reference center in Bogotá during the 2024-2025 period. We included 494 women, 18 years or older, who had undergone abdominal computed tomography. Double reading by residents was applied, with 2-of-3 majority adjudication between the resident and two independent expert reviewers. Statistical analysis included 95% Wilson confidence intervals, Cohen's kappa with Landis-Koch interpretation, and sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value, reported in accordance with STROBE guidelines. RESULTS: Resident-diagnosed prevalence was 88 of 494 (17.8%; 95% CI 14.7-21.4). Adjudicated prevalence was 83 of 494 (16.8%; 95% CI 13.8-20.4). Five cases (1.0%) were reclassified as extraperitoneal fat by expert consensus. Findings included indirect inguinal predominance, bilateral distribution in 26.1%, a high proportion of occult hernias, and underreporting in the original radiology report. Resident sensitivity was 100% against both expert reviewers. Specificity was 84.4% against Reviewer 1 and 47.4% against Reviewer 2. Cohen's kappa for resident vs. Reviewer 1 was 0.878; resident vs. Reviewer 2 was 0.326; and Reviewer 1 vs. Reviewer 2 was 0.408. CONCLUSIONS: The radiological prevalence in women sits above the classical clinical range. Extraperitoneal fat is an overlooked differential diagnosis in female cohorts and accounts for a large part of interreviewer discordance. The 2-of-3 rule works as a replicable method for diagnostic studies with limited resources.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Language difficulties are a prevalent developmental concern, but prognostic heterogeneity makes early identification of high-risk children challenging. This study aimed to investigate factors associated with language difficulties and to identify early predictors of special educational needs (SEN) in Turkish-speaking children. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary paediatric hospital in Türkiye. The analytical cohort for the analysis of factors associated with language difficulties consisted of 255 children with language difficulties and 51 children who were judged to have typical development after evaluation, all initially referred for speech delay between May 2014 and May 2021. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent associations. RESULTS: In the multivariable model, later age at presentation (adjusted OR 1.08 per month, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.16) and vitamin D deficiency (adjusted OR 4.22, 95% CI 1.00 to 17.75) were significantly associated with language difficulties. Within the language difficulties cohort (n=255), children with SEN (n=88) presented at a later age (mean difference 8.6 months, 95% CI 5.5 to 11.6) and had higher odds of screen exposure >2 hours/day (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.1 to 4.2) compared with those without SEN (n=154). CONCLUSIONS: Later age at presentation and vitamin D deficiency were associated with language difficulties, while later age at presentation and increased screen exposure were associated with SEN among children with language difficulties. These findings highlight the importance of early screening and suggest that modifiable factors like screen time may be valuable intervention targets. The role of vitamin D in language disorders requires further prospective investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Interactions between T cell receptors (TCRs), peptides, and human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) underlie antigen-specific T cell immunity. Despite substantial advances in prediction methods, accurate modeling of coupled TCR-peptide-HLA recognition remains underdeveloped, limiting applications such as TCR and neoepitope prioritization in cancer and antigen identification in autoimmunity. Here we present StriMap, a unified framework for predicting TCR-peptide-HLA interactions by integrating physicochemical, sequence-context, and structural features at recognition interfaces. StriMap achieves state-of-the-art performance with improved generalizability and enables applications in cancer and autoimmunity. As a case study, we screened 13 million peptides from 43,241 bacterial proteins and identified candidate molecular mimics that were experimentally validated to activate T cells expressing an ankylosing spondylitis (AS)-associated TCR. A top validated peptide was enriched in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), suggesting potential shared microbial triggers. Overall, StriMap provides a framework for rational immunotherapy design and dissecting antigenic drivers of autoimmunity.

papers.abstract_en: ClpP protease maintains proteostasis in human mitochondria and is overexpressed in cancers such as acute myeloid leukemia (AML). While activators such as dordaviprone (ONC201) have reached the clinic, the development of ClpP inhibitors has been hampered by paradoxical activation upon orthosteric inhibitor binding. Here, we report a series of quinazolinone-based compounds that allosterically inhibit human ClpP with nanomolar potency. Cryo-EM and H/D exchange mass spectrometry reveal that our lead compound binds sub-stoichiometrically to a distal hydrophobic pocket ~30 Å from the active sites, disrupts a conserved inter-subunit cluster, and induces a conformational change that misaligns the catalytic triad, thereby inactivating ClpP. The binding site of our quinazolinone-based inhibitors partially overlaps with that of the activator dordaviprone. In a xenograft mouse model of leukemia, our lead compound significantly reduced tumor burden following short-term oral administration. papers.abstract_en: The world is stochastic, making planning difficult. Despite the ubiquity of stochasticity in real-world environments, it remains an open question how people effectively balance the cognitive costs of planning against its potential benefits when faced with stochasticity. To study this, we designed a planning task where participants face one of three forms of stochasticity commonly encountered in the real world: reliability, volatility, and controllability. We find a robust pattern across all three manipulations: as stochasticity increases, people reduce their planning effort as measured by first-choice response times. To understand the processes underlying this effect, we developed several computational cognitive models to account for participants' choices. We find that rather than calculating expected values optimally, people choose a simpler strategy, acting as if the world were deterministic, a phenomenon known as determinizing. Consistent with our response time findings, we find that people reduce their effort by decreasing their sensitivity to values with increasing stochasticity, a signature of policy compression. Our work highlights the often overlooked role of stochasticity in human planning and its impact on planning strategy and effort. Moreover, it reveals the limitations of studying stochasticity solely through single-shot decisions.

papers.abstract_en: Carboxylases are among the most important enzymes in nature as they catalyze the fixation of inorganic carbon (CO2), a central step in the global carbon cycle. In addition to their well-known function in autotrophic CO2 fixation, many carboxylases play a role in the heterotrophic assimilation of organic compounds. In this study, we provide genomic evidence for an assimilatory carboxylation pathway involved in acetone degradation in photoheterotrophic bacteria from metagenomes collected along a latitudinal transect of the Arctic Ocean. This curious metabolism was linked to a single population of Gammaproteobacteria (Porticoccus arcticus). P. arcticus has a streamlined genome compared to Porticoccus relatives but has maintained a complete acetone carboxylation pathway while acquiring multiple proteorhodopsin genes by lateral gene transfer. Arctic Ocean metatranscriptomes revealed the acetone carboxylase and rhodopsins genes were among the most highly expressed P. arcticus genes in oligotrophic Arctic surface waters. P. arcticus sequences were consistently detected, and often abundant (up to 9%), in a multiyear Arctic Ocean 16S rRNA time-series, supporting its ecological significance in Arctic marine systems. Overall, this work reports a metabolic module (acetone carboxylation) in the ocean that may allow photoheterotrophic bacteria to enhance their biosynthetic capacity via CO2 assimilation.

papers.abstract_en: Piezoelectric surface acoustic wave devices can drive charge carriers in semiconductors through the acoustoelectric effect, generating direct currents with potential applications in sensing and biomedicine. These results establish a wireless acoustoelectric platform for stable, tunable, and miniaturized current delivery, suggesting potential for biomedical applications.

papers.abstract_en: Diurnal asymmetric warming profoundly affects lake thermodynamics and aquatic ecosystems, yet its large-scale patterns and drivers remain poorly understood. Here we analyze diurnal surface temperature trends of 613 lakes across China from 2001 to 2025, disentangling climatic and anthropogenic contributions. Nighttime warming drives long-term lake warming nationally, with 84.01% of lakes showing a nighttime-dominant pattern. Nighttime lake surface water temperature (LSWT) rose at +0.34 °C decade-1, while daytime LSWT cooled at -0.24 °C decade-1. Lake area expansion correlates negatively with daytime warming and positively with nighttime warming nationwide, while anthropogenic activity further amplifies this asymmetry, most strongly in the Eastern Plain lakes. These findings highlight nighttime warming as the dominant force in Chinese lake thermal evolution, informing future conservation and management.

papers.abstract_en: Targeted biomolecular modification requires recognizing and binding to extended sequence domains, which can limit product dissociation rates and, therefore, catalytic efficiency. Product removal by downstream enzymes or condensates, common in biological catalysis, pushes catalytic reactions toward product formation, but cannot overcome intrinsically low product off-rates. Here, we demonstrate that designed affinity reagents, termed scavengers, can actively displace a product from an enzyme. Designed scavengers for three nucleic acid enzymes increase catalytic turnover up to 39-fold. Additionally, co-localizing enzymes and substrates, but not scavengers, within a biomolecular condensate further enhances >6-fold in catalytic rate by biasing productive substrate-enzyme interaction over inhibitory substrate-scavenger complexation. Scavenging and colocalization can be combined into a single generalizable and programmable framework, multiphase-controlled product scavenging (MCPS). By enabling rapid and exquisitely specific biomolecular modification, MCPS could lead to the development of potent nucleic acid enzyme therapeutics or efficient, controllable pathways for biomolecular modification, cleavage, and synthesis.

Last, individuals with potent and neutralizing antibodies and IFN-γ+ T cells at baseline experienced minimal viral replication. Together, these findings demonstrate that controlled human challenge with dengue virus can delineate coordinated versus dysregulated acute immune responses and their effects on immunogenicity, informing therapeutic and vaccine strategies for dengue and other viral diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is emerging as the leading cause of chronic liver disease, posing a global public health challenge without available therapeutic approaches. Protein arginine methyltransferase 6 is a type I PRMT that asymmetrically dimethylates arginine residues of a variety of substrates implicated in many diseases. However, its role in NAFLD pathologies has not been clarified. In this study, we show that PRMT6 is upregulated in NAFLD and NASH of mice and human patients. Prmt6-deficient mice are protected from diet-induced hepatic steatosis, steatohepatitis, insulin resistance, and glucose tolerance. Mechanistically, PRMT6 interacts with and dimethylates Forkhead box K1 (FOXK1) at four conserved arginine residues (R161, R191, R259, and R486), maintaining its nuclear localization and transcriptional activity as a repressor/activator, inhibiting fatty acid oxidation and stimulating lipogenesis programs, respectively. PRMT6 competes with glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK3) for binding to FOXK1 and triggers FOXK1 methylation. This methylation prevents FOXK1 from GSK3-mediated phosphorylation, leading to its dissociation from 14-3-3, enhanced nuclear retention, and transcriptional activity. Conversely, the methylation-defective FOXK1 mutant (4RK) has the opposite effect and confers resistance to diet-induced hepatic steatosis in mice. Moreover, pharmacological inhibition of PRMT6 by EPZ020411 ameliorates NAFLD progression in mice. Thus, our study demonstrates the PRMT6-FOXK1 axis as a critical regulator of NAFLD and that targeting PRMT6 represents a novel therapeutic intervention for NAFLD.

papers.abstract_en: Various approaches have been explored to address the on-target, off-tissue toxicity of PROTACs and molecular glues, but most fall short in achieving robust in vivo selectivity and efficacy. papers.abstract_en: Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm infections pose a severe clinical challenge due to antibiotic resistance driven by quorum sensing (QS). This work establishes 2g as a machine learning-optimized LasR inhibitor with potent antibiofilm activity and synergistic antibiotic enhancement, offering a translatable strategy against multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa infections.

papers.abstract_en: Macrophages within advanced atherosclerotic lesions typically exhibit impaired efferocytosis and tend to adopt a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype, leading to the progression of atherosclerosis. Despite this challenge, the development of biocompatible nanotherapeutics capable of effectively remodeling macrophage efferocytosis and phenotype remains elusive. Here, we developed engineered targeted-peptide-modified nanocarriers (PP) and demonstrated their potential to restore macrophage efferocytosis while promoting re-polarization towards an anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotype. This study not only underscores the new pleiotropic effects of PP to restore macrophage efferocytosis and modulate macrophage phenotype, but also highlights the promising potential of PP for the treatment of atherosclerosis and diseases associated with macrophage dysfunction.

papers.abstract_en: Anti-hypertensive (anti-HTN) drugs are widely prescribed, but the features of associated drug-induced liver injury (DILI) are poorly defined. A total of 2207 patients enrolled in the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network (DILIN) from 2003 to 2024 were adjudicated as definite, highly likely, or probable DILI. Of these, 44 cases were attributed to anti-HTN drugs. These were compared with non-anti-HTN DILI cases and population controls. Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) sequencing was performed, and allele frequencies were analyzed using Fisher's Exact Test. Among the 44 anti-HTN DILI cases, 14 were caused by ACE inhibitors/ARBs, 13 by methyldopa, 11 by hydralazine, and 3 each by beta-blockers and calcium-channel blockers. Methyldopa DILI presented with hepatocellular injury in young women (prescribed mainly for pregnancy-related HTN). Non-methyldopa cases were 60% hepatocellular, 28% cholestatic, and 9% mixed. Severe outcomes included two liver transplants and two deaths (lisinopril and hydralazine). HLA-B∗35:01 was markedly enriched (50% vs. 13% in controls; OR 6.0; P = 1 × 10-8) and was linked to shorter latency (50 vs. 109 days; P = 0.02) but not severity. HLA-B∗35:01 was overrepresented across all drug classes, including 66% of methyldopa cases, 27% of hydralazine cases, and 42% of ACE/ARB cases. DILI from anti-HTN medications is very rare but strongly associated with HLA-B∗35:01, especially for methyldopa. Carriers display a shorter latency, potentially indicating an accelerated adaptive immune response, that warrants further exploration.

papers.abstract_en: Atypical sensory processing is commonly observed in autism, particularly when integration across sensory modalities is required. The neural mechanisms underlying multisensory differences remain unclear. We recorded EEG while autistic children aged 8-13 (AU;n = 40), siblings of autistic children (SIB;n = 26), and non-autistic controls (NA;n = 36) performed a simple reaction-time task to auditory (A), visual (V), and audiovisual (AV) stimuli. Analyses targeted event-related potentials (ERPs), alpha-band event-related desynchronization (α-ERD), and long-range theta-band functional connectivity. Groups did not differ across unisensory measures, indicating comparable unisensory processing. By contrast, multisensory integration (MSI;AV-(A+V)) differed across groups: NA children showed significant ERP MSI over parieto-central sites that was absent in AU and SIB; and α-ERD MSI was significantly reduced in AU, with SIB showing an intermediate profile. Connectivity analyses revealed reduced AV fronto-parieto-occipital coupling in autistic children relative to non-autistic children, suggesting weaker large-scale coordination during multisensory processing. These results point to a multisensory-specific deficit spanning early sensory encoding, posterior α-ERD, and fronto-posterior coupling and support disrupted multisensory influences on sensory processing due to reduced multisensory attentional orienting. SIB profiles suggest inherited liability for these neural phenotypes. These results help explain well-documented behavioral MSI differences in autism by linking impaired early enhancement with attenuated top-down control of sensory cortex.

papers.abstract_en: The Josephson junction (JJ) is the fundamental nonlinear building block of superconducting quantum technologies. Its macroscopic quantum tunneling physics underpins superconducting quantum computing, sensing, and communication, but scaling these platforms to utility-scale architectures places increasingly stringent demands on junction materials, interfaces, and fabrication. Practical quantum computing requires high reproducibility, low power consumption, tunability, a small device footprint, and resilience to noise and defects. This review surveys how advances in materials science, device characterization, and nanofabrication are addressing these challenges and redefining the figures of merit for next-generation JJs. This review also examines the evolution of fabrication strategies, from conventional multi-angle evaporation to foundry-compatible superconducting processes and the integration of emerging junction materials. Progress along these directions will determine how rapidly JJs move from laboratory-scale components to the foundation of industrial-scale quantum processors.

papers.abstract_en: Myofiber hypertrophy is central to economically important agricultural traits and vertebrate development, yet the underlying cellular and molecular programs remain elusive. Chickens have undergone substantial divergence in muscle growth following decades of artificial selection, making them a unique model for dissecting these mechanisms at single-cell resolution. Here, we performed singlenucleus RNA sequencing on 91 144 nuclei from postnatal chicken pectoralis major. Eight major conserved cell populations were resolved, with temporal dynamics exhibiting divergence between fast-growing broilers and slow-growing layers. A novel terminally differentiated myocyte subpopulation (AK1+ myocytes) was markedly enriched in slow-growing birds. Analysis revealed that accelerated myoblast expansion and delayed terminal differentiation are primary drivers of myofiber hypertrophy, supported by a pro-growth niche involving IGF-signaling FAPs and macrophage-myogenic crosstalk. Further comprehensive analyses identified CREM as a master repressor of myofiber hypertrophy. Mechanistically, CREM directly binds and transcriptionally activates the JUN promoter, and both factors cooperatively sustain the expression of growth inhibitors MSTN, FBXO32, and TRIM63. In vivo and in vitro functional validation confirmed that CREM deletion promotes myofiber hypertrophy, increasing pectoralis major weight and percent by 29.96% and 20.50%, respectively. This study uncovers CREM as a novel brake on myofiber hypertrophy, offering fundamental insights into vertebrate skeletal muscle development.

papers.abstract_en: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. Leveraging data augmentation and ensemble modeling, we use a hierarchical neural network to predict ∼1 billion candidate formulations, balancing mechanical properties, optical transparency, and environmental footprint. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

papers.abstract_en: Stimuli-responsive nanomaterials offer powerful capabilities for neuromodulation, yet there is a continuous need for more versatile methods to ensure cell-specific targeting, a prerequisite for their precise application in neuroscience. papers.abstract_en: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. Using a storyline approach, we show that precipitation associated with Storm Boris would have been 6 to 9% lower in the absence of anthropogenic climate change, whereas flood peaks would, on average, have been reduced by 14 to 22%. Our estimates are based on nudged simulations from two climate models coupled with two hydrological models across hundreds of affected catchments. The results imply that anthropogenic forcing amplified flood peaks by a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 relative to the increase in event precipitation. Overall, we demonstrate that attributing precipitation alone would substantially underestimate flood hazard amplification from climate change-an effect that should inform future risk assessments and loss estimates.

papers.abstract_en: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

papers.abstract_en: The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. papers.abstract_en: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth's history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

papers.abstract_en: 3D bioprinting is essential for constructing functional tissue mimics but remains challenging due to the difficulty of simultaneously achieving adequate cell-cell interactions and appropriate biomaterial support. Here, we introduce a cell-driven clustering strategy that assembles hydrogel microparticles into cell-rich aggregates, in which cells occupy the interstitial spaces and establish pre-organized cellular interactions prior to printing. papers.abstract_en: Neuropathic pain remains a major clinical challenge owing to complex neuroimmune mechanisms and limited disease-modifying therapies. Neuroinflammation within the dorsal root ganglion (DRG), particularly macrophage infiltration and pro-inflammatory polarization, is a key driver of sensory neuronal sensitization and pain persistence. Here, we report an injectable reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive natural drug self-delivery hydrogel for localized and sustained treatment of neuropathic pain. Single-cell transcriptomic reanalysis revealed marked macrophage accumulation in injured DRGs, accompanied by M1-like polarization and aberrant phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-Akt activation. Mechanism-guided virtual screening identified glycyrrhizic acid (GA), a bioactive natural product, as a promising PI3K-targeting candidate. To improve local bioavailability, GA was engineered into a 1,4-phenylenediboronic acid (1,4-PBA)-functionalized self-assembled hydrogel, termed GA-PBA-GA (GPG), through dynamic boronate ester bonds and non-covalent interactions. The GPG hydrogel exhibited injectability, self-healing, biodegradability, biocompatibility, and inflammation-associated ROS-triggered GA release. In vitro, GPG suppressed PI3K-Akt signaling, reduced pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, and promoted M1-to-M2 repolarization. In a rat model of L5 spinal nerve ligation-induced neuropathic pain, peri-DRG administration alleviated mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity, improved gait and electrophysiological function, reduced DRG macrophage-mediated neuroinflammation, and attenuated spinal microglial activation. This ROS-responsive natural drug self-delivery hydrogel provides a minimally invasive strategy for remodeling DRG neuroinflammation and achieving sustained relief of neuropathic pain through localized drug delivery.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nasotracheal intubation is a common procedure for infants undergoing surgery, and successful intubation at first attempt reduces the risk of complications. First-attempt success is improved with videolaryngoscopy compared with direct laryngoscopy in infants requiring orotracheal intubation, but the value of videolaryngoscopy in infants requiring nasotracheal intubation is unknown. We aimed to compare first-attempt success of nasotracheal intubation by videolaryngoscopy and direct laryngoscopy in infants undergoing cardiac procedures. METHODS: In this multicentre, parallel group, randomised controlled trial across eight paediatric cardiac centres in the USA, we enrolled infants aged 365 days or younger without anticipated difficult airways requiring nasotracheal intubation for elective cardiothoracic surgery or cardiac catheterisation. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to videolaryngoscopy or direct laryngoscopy using permuted block randomisation stratified by site. The primary outcome was first-attempt intubation success rate. Analysis was by modified intention to treat using generalised estimating equations to account for clustering within intubating clinicians. Complications associated with first attempt and across all attempts were compared between groups with the same marginal models as the primary outcome analysis. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05433155) and is closed to new participants. FINDINGS: Between July 1, 2022, and March 31, 2024, 684 infants were randomly assigned, of whom 673 were included in the primary outcome analysis: 340 in the videolaryngoscopy group and 333 in the direct laryngoscopy group. 311 (46%) participants were female, 362 (54%) were male, and 457 (68%) were White. The median age was 14·04 weeks (IQR 1·48-22·89) and the mean weight was 4·77 kg (SD 1·74). First-attempt success was higher in the videolaryngoscopy group than in the direct laryngoscopy group (281 [83%] vs 249 [75%]; adjusted risk difference 8·2% [95% CI 2·0-14·3], p=0·0093). First-attempt complications occurred in 85 (13%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (45 [13%] vs 40 [12%]; 0·4% [-3·5 to 4·3], p=0·83). Considering all attempts cumulatively, any complication occurred in 94 (14%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (46 [14%] vs 48 [14%]; -1·9% [-6·0 to 2·3], p=0·38). No cases of cardiac arrest or death occurred in either group. INTERPRETATION: Improved first-attempt success rates with videolaryngoscopy for nasotracheal intubation in infants undergoing cardiac procedures add to growing evidence favouring videolaryngoscopy as the first-line technique for tracheal intubation in infants. Key remaining questions for ongoing research include whether this benefit extends to infants with difficult airways and at non-specialist centres or urgent settings, and how clinician training should evolve as videolaryngoscopy becomes standard practice. papers.abstract_en: Colonic drug delivery has the potential to provide therapeutic benefit for diseases like Ulcerative Colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD) by elevating local drug concentrations while minimizing adverse effects associated with systemic exposure. Achieving colonic drug delivery requires deliberate formulation development optimally supported by Physiologically Based Biopharmaceutics Models (PBBMs) that may predict colonocyte exposure and drug concentration in the colon lumen. In this study, ritlecitinib (Litfulo™), a covalent inhibitor of JAK3 and TEC family kinases, was incorporated into modified release (MR) lipid microsphere formulations to achieve colonic delivery. To assess in vivo performance, two ritlecitinib MR formulations were administered to healthy human volunteers, pre- and post-prandially, and a ritlecitinib oral solution was administered as a control. Using a combination of the resulting pharmacokinetic dataset, ritlecitinib physicochemical properties, in vitro release profiles of the administered formulations, and formulation-specific gastrointestinal transit profiles, a PBBM was established to predict the ritlecitinib dose fraction absorbed in each gastrointestinal compartment, pre- and post-prandially. In the fasted state, the ritlecitinib dose fraction absorbed in the colon (Facolon) was enhanced for both the faster-releasing (Facolon: 0.38 ± 0.07) and slower-releasing (Facolon: 0.40 ± 0.08) MR formulations relative to the oral solution (Facolon: 0.01 ± 0.01). In the fed state, Facolon was consistent for the slower-releasing formulation (Facolon: 0.38 ± 0.07), whereas Facolon for the faster-releasing formulation was notably reduced (Facolon: 0.27 ± 0.09), indicating that consistent colonic delivery across prandial states depends on release rate optimization. papers.abstract_en: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations have enabled the in vivo delivery of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccines and therapeutics yet the delivery of RNA remains relatively inefficient. In order to improve LNP design there is a need to better understand how current mRNA-LNP formulations are trafficked and expressed in vivo. Importantly, no prior work has quantified mRNA-LNP transport through lymphatics. In the current study we profile the thoracic lymph uptake, plasma pharmacokinetics (PK), and tissue protein expression after intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration in rats of three common LNP formulations (ALC-0315, SM-102 and MC3 ionizable lipids) containing muGFP-P2A-nLuc reporter mRNA. After IV administration, the SM-102 and MC3 LNP formulations provided the most effective protection of mRNA in plasma. Despite this, tissue NanoLuc® Luciferase (nLuc) expression at 32 h post-dosing was relatively similar across formulations with highest expression seen in the liver and spleen. After SC injection, all formulations supported relatively low bioavailability of mRNA (0.42-0.87% dose) and slightly higher bioavailability of ionizable and PEG lipid (<5% dose) with PK profiles of the ionizable lipid and PEG lipid not completely matching the mRNA PK profiles. There was also greater lymphatic recovery of all ionizable lipids (3.1-4.3% dose) compared to mRNA (0.62-1.4% dose) and PEG lipid (1.9-2.0% dose). Together this data suggests that mRNA is lost prior to or during lymphatic transport. Importantly, concentrations of all mRNA-LNP components were 10-1000 fold higher in thoracic lymph compared to plasma after SC injection. At 32 h after SC injection, highest nLuc expression was seen in lymph nodes and tissues near the dosing site and in the liver and spleen. These findings demonstrating that mRNA-LNPs predominantly traffic from tissue injection sites via lymphatics, mRNA-LNP components may traffic separately from each other in both lymph and blood, and tissue protein expression reflects the PK of mRNA-LNPs at early timepoints.

papers.abstract_en: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has improved clinical outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve durable responses, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory inhibitor subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a metabolic driver of immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC through RNA sequencing of tumors with differential responses to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy. Mechanistically, PPP1R1B directly interacted with IRF3 through the Arg29 residue and promoted dephosphorylation of IRF3 at Ser396, thereby suppressing IRF3 activation and downstream interferon-β (IFN-β) signaling. PPP1R1B-mediated inhibition of IFN-β signaling reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and impaired antitumor immunity, ultimately conferring resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in vivo. Blockade of IFN-β signaling abrogated the antitumor effects induced by PPP1R1B depletion, supporting an immune-dependent mechanism. Notably, tumors resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy exhibited impaired oxidative phosphorylation and excessive lactate accumulation. Lactate induced PPP1R1B expression through NF-κB-dependent transcriptional activation, linking metabolic reprogramming to innate immune suppression. Collectively, our findings identify a lactate/NF-κB/PPP1R1B/IRF3 signaling axis that drives immune evasion and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in NSCLC, and nominate PPP1R1B as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Core binding factor acute myeloid leukemia (CBF-AML) driven by the CBFB-MYH11 fusion oncogene is associated with high initial remission rates, yet 30%–50% of patients ultimately relapse. While immune evasion is a recognized hallmark of leukemia progression, the precise mechanisms orchestrated by the CBFB-MYH11 oncogene remain poorly understood. Furthermore, the role of transforming growth factor-beta (TGFβ) in hematological malignancies is highly controversial, often viewed as a tumor suppressor in early hematopoiesis rather than a driver of immune evasion. METHODS: We used an inducible Cbfb-MYH11 knock-in mouse model and primary AML cell transplantation to profile the immune microenvironment during leukemogenesis. We integrated flow cytometry, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), CUT&RUN, luciferase reporter assay, ChIP-qPCR, and ChIP-Seq. Functional in vitro T-cell suppression assays and in vivo engraftment using Pdcd1 knockout (PD-1 KO) mice, and treatments with the anti-PD-L1 antibody, TGFβ receptor inhibitor galunisertib, and cytarabine were performed to evaluate immunotherapeutic vulnerabilities. RESULTS: Leukemogenesis in the Cbfb-MYH11 model was accompanied by profound T-cell suppression and exhaustion, and the AML cells effectively inhibited T-cell proliferation in co-culture. Transcriptomic profiling identified marked upregulation of Cd274 (PD-L1) and Tgfb1 in AML cells. Mechanistically, CUT&RUN and ChIP-Seq demonstrated that the CBFβ-SMMHC fusion oncoprotein and its co-factor RUNX1 directly bind to the promoter regions of CD274 and TGFB1 to transcriptionally activate their expression in both murine and human AML models. While genetic ablation of PD-1 in host mice provided only limited survival benefits, pharmacological blockade of TGFβ effectively restored T cell function and delayed AML progression. Importantly, combining cytarabine with galunisertib provided superior disease control, reversed T cell exhaustion, and significantly prolonged survival compared with chemotherapy alone, which can be further enhanced by targeting PD-L1/PD-1. CONCLUSIONS: The CBFB-MYH11 oncogene directly orchestrates an immunosuppressive microenvironment by transcriptionally activating PD-L1 and TGFβ. These findings provide more insight into the role of TGFβ in CBF-AML, establishing it as a primary, tumor-derived immunosuppressor directly driven by the fusion oncogene. This provides a strong mechanistic rationale for incorporating TGFβ blockade into standard chemotherapy and immune checkpoint blockade regimens to restore anti-leukemic immunity and prevent relapse.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: CD30+ T cell lymphoproliferative disorders (CD30+ T LPD) with cutaneous involvement comprise a diverse group of neoplasms with variable clinical outcomes. METHODS: In this multi-institutional retrospective study, 79 patients with CD30+ T LPD were evaluated. DNA and RNA sequencing were performed on skin biopsy samples to characterise molecular features. Furthermore, immune microenvironment deconvolution showed a higher abundance of resting dendritic cells in the low-risk group. Finally, high-risk patients exhibited significant overexpression of clinically relevant proteins, highlighting potential alternative treatment approaches for this population. INTERPRETATION: Mutation analyses suggest diverse pathogenesis in these diseases. The high-risk and low-risk groups diverge in gene expression profiles and immune microenvironment, suggesting that these biological differences hold prognostic significance. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) drives intestinal barrier dysfunction, endotoxemia, and liver injury, yet the epithelial mechanisms remain undefined. Autophagy and lysosomes maintain intestinal epithelial homoeostasis and barrier integrity, but their response to chronic alcohol exposure is unclear. METHODS: Human intestinal tissues from individuals with and without AUD were analysed alongside human intestinal organoids. Wild-type, CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3, GFP-LC3B, and Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice underwent chronic-binge ethanol feeding. Organoids and Caco-2 cells were exposed to ethanol (50 mM) with or without bafilomycin A1 or Torin-2. Autophagy-lysosome pathways were assessed using transcriptomics, immunofluorescence, biochemical fractionation, and flux reporters. FINDINGS: Alcohol induced heterogeneous autophagy-lysosome responses characterised by lysosomal stress/adaptive remodelling. These changes occurred with limited autophagosome formation and maturation, resulting in impaired autophagic throughput. These responses differed along the crypt-villus axis and between intestinal regions. Disrupted autophagy was associated with altered trafficking and accumulation of claudin-2. Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice exhibited increased baseline intestinal permeability vs wild-type controls (p = 0.03). Following ethanol exposure, Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice showed greater intestinal permeability (p = 0.003), circulating and hepatic endotoxin (p = 0.002), hepatic triglycerides (p = 0.01), and serum ALT (p = 0.02) vs ethanol-fed wild-type mice. INTERPRETATION: Alcohol disrupts intestinal autophagy-lysosome homoeostasis in a spatially heterogeneous manner, accompanied by defective epithelial proteostasis and tight junction dysregulation. Impaired autophagosome formation exacerbates gut permeability and liver injury, supporting intestinal autophagy as a potential therapeutic target in alcohol-associated disease. Broader applicability of the human findings requires validation in larger cohorts. FUNDING: This study was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder (CANS) are disorders that develop as a result of repetitive movements, awkward postures or external forces (e.g. vibrating tools), and significantly affect the working population globally. Ergonomic interventions (which aim to enhance efficiency and comfort in the working environment) can be used to manage CANS. This review is based on a new protocol but updates part of a 2013 Cochrane review. OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of ergonomic interventions for work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder (CANS) in adults, in terms of their effects on pain, functional status and work-related outcomes. SEARCH METHODS: We updated the 2013 review searches, searching from 31 May 2013 to 1 June 2026 in eight bibliographic databases and one trials register. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), cluster-RCTs and quasi-RCTs that evaluated single or combined ergonomic interventions (e.g. office furniture, biomechanical or ergonomic education) compared to no treatment/usual care/placebo or another active intervention (exercise/another ergonomic intervention/other treatment), or as an add-on treatment. OUTCOMES: Critical outcomes: pain, functional status (disability) and work-related outcomes (e.g. sickness absence, return to work, productivity loss at work, change of occupation). Important outcomes: global perceived effect (e.g. overall improvement), quality of life, healthcare consumption, and recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. We prioritised outcomes in the short term (up to three months after the intervention) and were also interested in long-term results (over three months). RISK OF BIAS: We assessed the risk of bias in the studies using Cochrane's RoB 1 tool. SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two authors independently screened the search records, selected trials, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. When we judged studies to have sufficient clinical and statistical homogeneity, we performed meta-analysis. We assessed overall certainty of the evidence using GRADE for key outcomes at the short-term time point. INCLUDED STUDIES: We brought forward 13 studies from the 2013 review. We identified two new articles relating to one of those 13 studies, along with seven new studies. Therefore, in total, we included 20 studies involving 2478 participants. In 16 studies, the participants had non-specific CANS; in four studies, the participants had specific CANS (e.g. carpal tunnel syndrome). SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Results below are presented at the short-term time point. Ergonomic interventions versus no treatment, usual care or placebo in people with CANS Data were available only for trials that focused on non-specific CANS. Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in pain compared to no treatment, usual care or placebo in people with CANS (SMD -0.23, 95% CI -0.54 to 0.08; 4 RCTs, 692 participants; low-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions probably result in little to no difference in functional status (disability) compared to being on a waiting list (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.34; 1 RCT (2 comparisons), 383 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in sick leave compared to no treatment (MD for continuous data -0.32, 95% CI -0.73 to 0.09; 1 RCT, 98 participants; low-certainty evidence; RR for dichotomous data 0.87, 95% CI 0.63 to 1.21; 3 RCTs, 759 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions probably result in little to no difference in recovery compared to no treatment (RR 1.32, 95% CI 0.89 to 1.97; 1 RCT (2 comparisons), 386 participants, moderate-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in quality of life compared to no treatment (MD 0.10, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.20; 1 RCT, 68 participants; low-certainty evidence). Ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in healthcare consumption compared to no treatment when measured using continuous outcomes (MD -0.10. 95% CI -0.30 to 0.10; 1 RCT, 68 participants; low-certainty evidence), and may result in a reduction in healthcare consumption compared to usual care when measured using dichotomous outcomes (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.31 to 0.78; 1 RCT, 210 participants; low-certainty evidence). No data were available for recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. Ergonomic intervention versus active intervention (exercise or another type of ergonomic intervention or other treatment) in people with CANS Data were available from trials involving participants with specific CANS and with non-specific CANS. The evidence is very uncertain about the effects of ergonomic interventions on pain (SMD 0.41, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.84; 8 RCTs, 364 participants; very-low-certainty evidence) and on functional status (disability) (SMD -0.09, 95% CI -0.85 to 0.68; 3 RCTs, 180 participants; very-low-certainty evidence) compared to active intervention in people with specific or non-specific CANS. Intense ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in recovery (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.94; 1 RCT, 257 participants; low-certainty evidence) or healthcare consumption (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.47; 1 RCT, 217 participants; low-certainty evidence) compared to ergonomic education in people with non-specific CANS. Ergonomic interventions may improve quality of life compared to exercise in people with non-specific CANS (MD -10.10, 95% CI -19.87 to -0.33; 1 RCT, 61 participants; low-certainty evidence). No data were available for work-related outcomes or recurrence of injury, disorder or complaint. Ergonomic intervention plus another treatment versus the other treatment alone in people with CANS Data were available only from trials of participants with non-specific CANS. The evidence is very uncertain about the effects of ergonomic intervention as an add-on treatment to exercise on pain (SMD -0.50, 95% CI -1.64 to 0.63; 2 RCTs, 137 participants; very-low-certainty evidence). No data were available for our other outcomes of interest. AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Overall, ergonomic interventions for work-related CANS may have no meaningful effects on pain, function, recovery, quality of life or work-related outcomes (sick leave) compared with no treatment or usual care. Findings are inconsistent for healthcare consumption. There may be a possible benefit for quality of life when ergonomic interventions are compared to exercise. The evidence for ergonomic interventions as an add-on treatment is very uncertain. High-quality, well-designed trials are needed to establish the role of ergonomic interventions in the management of CANS.
