papers.abstract_en: Quantum sensing technologies offer unprecedented detection sensitivities down to single-molecule, attomolar detection limits and thus are emerging as transformative tools for ultra-sensitive biomarker detection in biomedical diagnostics. This comprehensive review synthesizes insights from over 380 plus studies to provide recent advances in quantum sensor platforms, examining the fundamental quantum mechanical principles that enable enhanced sensitivity, and surveys a diverse range of quantum sensing technologies along with their applications across the biomedical field. Specifically, nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, quantum dots, superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs), and other quantum sensing modalities applied to biomarker detection for cancer diagnostics, cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, and infectious disease detection are reviewed. Further, the key technical challenges that hurdle their clinical translation are critically evaluated. The review results demonstrate that quantum-enhanced biosensors have achieved detection limits of the order of magnitude below conventional methods. Intrinsic to their capabilities, several quantum sensing platforms have progressed to clinical testing and early commercialization efforts. Specifically, for point-of-care diagnosis, early disease detection, and personalized medicine.

papers.abstract_en: Fine synthesis of oriented metal oxide nanoarrays with tailored chemical compositions is highly desirable for the development of high-performance sensing nanodevices. However, conventional methods normally struggle to diversify the composition of metal oxide nanoarrays. Herein, a micellar brush-directed surface-confined sequential synthesis method is presented for the controlled fabrication of well-aligned metal oxide nanoarrays with designable constitutions via orderly decoupling the nucleation and growth process. The micellar brush provides an orient-confined space for promoting the nucleation-like process of various metal precursors (e.g., polyoxometalates and organometallic alcoholates), followed by programmable calcination to in situ convert into upright metal oxide nanoarrays, including WO3, MoO3, TiO2, Ta2O5, Nb2O5, and ZrO2 nanoarrays. Furthermore, the pyridine-rich micellar brush shells also readily bond with desired metal ions to enable the uniform doping of metal atoms into the metal oxide nanoarrays during the pyrolysis process. This endows metal oxide nanoarrays with tailored single-atom doping and abundant oxygen vacancies. Notably, the as-fabricated Cu-WO3 nanoarray exhibits competent H2S detection ability with high response (Ra/Rg = 168 for 10 ppm of H2S) and fast response-recovery (2.2/143 s) dynamics. Theoretical calculations further identify the presence of synergistic effects between single-atom Cu and oxygen vacancies, in which single atom Cu sites dominate H2S adsorption and oxygen vacancies facilitate oxygen activation. This work offers guidelines for the rational design of advanced metal oxide nanoarrays toward high-performance gas-sensing devices.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a X-linked disease affecting skeletal and cardiac muscle and is caused by mutations in the dystrophin gene (DMD). Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) serve as reliable in vitro disease models. Their genetic correction by CRISPR/Cas9 allows the generation of isogenic controls and holds promises for gene therapy. However, restoring full-length dystrophin, especially when deletions involve multiple exons, constitutes a technological challenge. This study aimed to fully repair the dystrophin gene from a DMD iPSC line carrying the deletion of exons 49-50 and to characterize the rescue of the cardiac phenotype. METHODS: We developed an innovative CRISPR/Cas9-based approach involving the insertion of coding sequences of the deleted region, at the 3' of exon 48, thereby generating a single continuous coding sequence encompassing exons 48-49-50. Subsequently, iPSCs were differentiated into cardiomyocytes and cardiac fibroblasts. Cardiac phenotypes were analysed by western blot, immunofluorescence, ELISA, FACS, Ionoptix, 3D engineered heart tissue (EHT) and single-nuclei RNA-seq. RESULTS: The correction of a two-exons DMD gene deletion in Duchenne iPSCs, using CRISPR/Cas9, enabled the re-expression of a stable and functional full-length dystrophin in cardiomyocytes resulting in the rescue of cardiac pathological phenotypes. Edited cardiomyocytes showed improved morphology, reduced release of the cardiomyocytes damage marker troponin I, and decreased ROS production. Moreover, dystrophin restoration enhanced contractility and ameliorated the Ca2+ kinetics. Notably, edited iPSC derived fibroblasts showed reduced pro-fibrotic stimuli response. In parallel, we also observed enhanced functioning of a 3D engineered heart tissue and profound change in the transcriptomic profile in both cardiomyocytes and fibroblasts after the re-expression of full-length dystrophin. CONCLUSIONS: We developed an innovative approach that enabled the re-expression of full-length dystrophin in a DMD iPSC line with consequent complete rescue of in vitro DMD cardiac phenotypes. On the long term, these results could lay a foundation for future applications of cell therapy or in vivo CRISPR/Cas9-based intervention to treat DMD.

papers.abstract_en: The ongoing emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants in an increasingly immune-experienced population is largely enabled by the plasticity of the Spike protein, which lies at the frontline of host immune pressure. Here, we investigated how extensive remodeling of the N-terminal domain (NTD) in Spike influences its antigenic properties. Using BA.2.87.1, a variant heavily mutated in this domain, we found that even large deletions do not substantially disrupt overall Spike structure or pseudovirus infectivity. However, our structural and binding analyses revealed that the NTD exhibits increased flexibility and that interaction with a heme-metabolite, known to facilitate the exposure of an immunodominant epitope, is lost. These conformational effects, coupled with 33 NTD mutations, compromised the ability of human convalescent antibodies to engage this domain, contributing to their reduced neutralizing capacity. Consequently, BA.2.87.1-like variants may escape recognition by the preexisting NTD-targeting antibodies, potentially reducing protection. Together, our results highlight the intrinsic adaptability of the Spike beyond the receptor-binding domain, with implications for immune escape during viral evolution.

papers.abstract_en: Stress hyperglycemia (SHG) predicts poor outcomes after myocardial infarction (MI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify FOXK2 as a key regulator of macrophage-mediated cardiac repair. Under high-glucose conditions, FOXK2 was glycosylated at T552 by O-GlcNAc transferase, promoting its ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation. Integrated CUT&Tag and RNA-seq analyses revealed that FOXK2 restrained pro-inflammatory cytokine expression by suppressing H3K27 acetylation. Thus, our findings identify FOXK2 as a critical regulator that supports cardiac repair during hyperglycemia, and targeting excessive FOXK2 O-GlcNAcylation may offer a therapeutic strategy for patients with MI and SHG.

papers.abstract_en: How sleep consolidates fear memories at the molecular level within individual engram neurons is unknown. Using activity-dependent tagging and sequencing, we profiled the DNA methylome and transcriptome of engram and non-engram nuclei from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) after contextual fear conditioning with and without post-learning sleep deprivation. Fear learning induces coordinated CpG and CpH DNA methylation remodeling specifically in engram neurons, with each showing unique temporal dynamics, revealing CpH methylation as a separate component of the engram's epigenetic signature. Interestingly, sleep deprivation partially reverses learning-induced methylation changes and impairs memory recall, indicating that sleep supports engram-specific epigenetic consolidation. Integrating the engram methylome with single-cell transcriptome profiling, we construct a multi-omic molecular atlas of the BLA fear engram and identify Mid1 as a learning- and sleep-regulated methylation target. BLA-wide and engram-specific Mid1 knockdown establishes its functional requirement for fear memory consolidation, providing an approach to identify behaviorally relevant epigenetic targets.

papers.abstract_en: Health inequalities are seen between populations, social groups in the same population and across populations ranked by social position. This paper focuses on trends in inequalities between countries and socio-economic inequalities in mortality within them. Mortality in most countries has improved since 1950 with some exceptions, notably: Younger adults in parts of Sub-Saharan Africa were associated with civil war, structural adjustment programmes and human immunodeficiency virus during the 1980s/1990s; the former USSR after the rapid adoption of neoliberal economic policies; European countries which implemented austerity in the 2010s; and globally in the shadow of COVID-19. Mortality differences between countries have narrowed, with the gap between the best and worst thirds of countries declining from 20.5 years for males and 22.6 years for females in 2000 to 15.6 years and 16.0 years, respectively, by 2021. Data for within-country inequalities are sparse and subject to measurement issues. Where trend data are available, they vary according to location and political context. For example, across many high-income countries, mortality inequalities improved in absolute terms between the 1990s and the early 2010s; however, relative inequalities widened. Inequalities in parts of Europe widened after 2012, reflecting austerity policies impacting the social and economic determinants of health, particularly for the poorest. Comparisons of between-country levels of inequality are problematic due to uncertainties of data recording and comparability; nonetheless, existing evidence demonstrates wider inequalities within particular 'neoliberal' political contexts. Future challenges include addressing such political determinants alongside the overlapping threats of climate change, social polarization, misinformation and erosion of democratic structures.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Non-operative management of acute Achilles tendon rupture (ATR) with early functional rehabilitation produces functional outcomes equivalent to surgery, but its effectiveness depends critically on patient compliance with bracing, weight-bearing and physiotherapy. Psychological factors, including motivation, self-efficacy, kinesiophobia, and social support, are plausible determinants of compliance and outcome, yet have received minimal systematic attention. SOURCES OF DATA: Seven databases were searched from inception to June 2026 without language restriction. Studies of adults with ATR managed non-operatively, with any psychological assessment reporting compliance, re-rupture rate, Achilles Tendon Total Rupture Score (ATRS) or return to sport, were eligible. Six studies met the inclusion criteria (797 non-operative patients in total), and two further non-operative randomized controlled trials were used for functional benchmarking only. Data were synthesized narratively (SWiM framework). AREAS OF AGREEMENT: Non-operative management with early functional rehabilitation yields ATRS scores of 72-86 at 6-12 months, comparable to operative cohorts, with re-rupture rates of 5%-12% under functional bracing. Treatment success depends on patient compliance, and functional deficits persist for years irrespective of the management modality. AREAS OF CONTROVERSY: Surgery continues to carry a lower re-rupture incidence than conservative management, although the absolute difference has narrowed with early functional rehabilitation. Whether pre-treatment psychological profiling should inform the choice between operative and non-operative management remains unvalidated, and no included study reported compliance as a formal outcome or its association with any psychological factor. GROWING POINTS: Kinesiophobia, anxiety, and depression are present throughout the first year of non-operative rehabilitation, and kinesiophobia scores above the clinical cut-off were observed in most participants of the only dedicated non-operative cohort. Kinesiophobia and readiness-to-return scores do not appear to differ between operatively and non-operatively managed patients, supporting a common psychological assessment framework. Qualitative evidence identifies motivation and social support as key facilitators of recovery. AREAS TIMELY FOR DEVELOPING RESEARCH: Future non-operative ATR randomized trials should incorporate the I-PRRS, TSK-11, and a validated motivation measure as pre-specified secondary outcomes, together with guideline-based compliance definitions. A prospective cohort study of baseline psychological profile as a predictor of compliance and re-rupture should be prioritized, followed by evaluation of simple psychological screening within consent and treatment-selection pathways.

papers.abstract_en: Synthetic consortia of Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae offer a powerful division-of-labor strategy for chemical biosynthesis. However, maintaining the stability of cross-species populations remains a major challenge. Here, we report an interspecific autonomous population-control platform for dynamically regulating Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae consortia. We found that the growth rate disparity between these two microorganisms leads to the suppression of yeast growth ultimately resulting in population imbalance and low biosynthesis. To overcome it, an E. coli auto-induction lysis circuit and a S. cerevisiae-driven cross-species lysis circuit were developed using salicylate-mediated intercellular signaling pathway to dynamic control the growth of E. coli in the consortia. papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Amanitin intoxication following ingestion of amatoxin-containing mushrooms can cause acute hepatic and renal failure. We evaluated the feasibility of using an adapted Patient Vital Status (PVS) fusion score derived from routine laboratory parameters to assess disease severity in amanitin-intoxicated patients. PVS was calculated using prothrombin time (Quick), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), bilirubin, and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), with predefined normal values and an intermediate-care reference group (n = 5) for severity scaling. RESULTS: Intoxicated patients had significantly higher maximum and mean PVS values than controls (PVSmax: 0.75 ± 0.54 vs. 0.12 ± 0.04; PVSmean: 0.32 ± 0.25 vs. 0.05 ± 0.02; mean ± standard deviation; both p < 0.001). Exploratory k-means clustering (k = 4) yielded four descriptive severity groups. The most severely affected patient reached a maximum PVS of 1.91 (ALT 10,373 U/L; AST 8,776 U/L; Quick 26.7%). Among patients with a matched ingestion time, the median time to peak PVS was 3.03 days (Q1-Q3, 2.13-3.54; n = 15). PVS was positively associated with Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) scores (p < 0.001). One patient died (last PVS 1.34). Urinary amanitin concentrations were not significantly associated with severity metrics. DISCUSSION: These findings support the feasibility of adapting PVS for longitudinal laboratory-based severity assessment in amanitin intoxication. Given the exploratory nature and limited sample size of this pilot study, validation in larger prospective cohorts is warranted.

papers.abstract_en: Severe acute hypermagnesemia from excessive magnesium (Mg2+) exposure is rare but life-threatening and requires prompt recognition. We report a 54-year-old previously healthy man who presented to the emergency department with acute altered consciousness and generalized weakness. Physical examination showed stupor, hypothermia, hypotension, and generalized areflexia. Initial laboratory testing demonstrated mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis, a normal serum creatinine concentration, and severe hypermagnesemia (serum Mg2+ concentration, 15.8 mg/dL). The initial 12-lead ECG demonstrated diffuse ST-segment depression, and an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) model identified an estimated mortality risk above the 99th percentile. Nasogastric decompression retrieved minimal gastric contents, and initial treatment with intravenous calcium, saline, and a loop diuretic did not produce meaningful neurological improvement. Emergent hemodialysis resulted in rapid recovery of consciousness and a decrease in serum Mg2+ to 4.9 mg/dL during treatment, together with neurological improvement and a marked decline in AI-ECG-predicted mortality risk. Subsequent history-taking indicated inadvertent ingestion of approximately 100 mL of a private-label artificial hot-spring mineral preparation, for which spa personnel reported a nominal formulation of 30% magnesium chloride, 33% magnesium sulfate, and 10% potassium sulfate. He recovered without residual complications. This case emphasizes that a normal serum creatinine concentration at presentation does not preclude life-threatening magnesium toxicity after a large acute Mg2+ exposure. Timely hemodialysis should be considered when severe symptoms persist despite initial therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX), a replacement for legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), is increasingly detected in the environment, yet its long-term toxicity remains poorly characterized. Current safety assessments rely largely on short-term, high-dose studies that may not capture the biological consequences of longer-term, low-dose exposure. To address this gap, we employed monocellular 3D HepG2/C3A hepatic spheroids cultured in a continuously rotating bioreactor system (ClinoStar) to systematically evaluate dose- and time-dependent mRNA changes in response to GenX under environmentally relevant conditions. Spheroids were exposed to GenX (0.08-50 μM, spanning environmentally relevant to mechanistically informative concentrations) for acute (4 days) and long-term (4 weeks) durations, followed by genome-wide TempO-Seq transcriptomic profiling and benchmark dose (BMD) modeling. Following actue exposure, the greatest number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) was observed at 0.4 μM, with fewer DEGs at higher concentrations. Long-term exposure produced a different concentration-dependent distribution of DEG with the greatest number observed at 50 μM. Notably, acute and long-term exposures elicited qualitatively distinct mRNA changes with low concordance across matched concentrations, demonstrating that exposure duration was a major determinant of mRNA changes. Acute low-dose GenX exposure preferentially modulated mRNA encoding components of cell cycle-related pathways, whereas acute higher dose exposures suppress mRNA levels of the transcripts encoding constituents of lipid metabolic pathways and increase expression of mRNA encoding proteins involved in stress- and toxicity-associated signaling. Long-term exposure revealed a different pattern of changes in mRNA expression not observed under acute exposure conditions, including suppression of mRNA expression levels of transcripts encoding cellular components involved in lipid-related pathways at the lowest concentration tested. At higher concentrations, mRNA levels encoding transcritps of components of multiple metabolic pathways were altered. Benchmark dose modeling identified a significantly lower transcriptomic point of departure (tPOD) for long-term exposure as compared to acute exposure, suggesting increased cellular response to prolonged GenX exposure and supporting the relevance of long-term models for human exposure assessment. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that GenX elicits distinct transcriptomic responses in HepG2/C3A spheroids depending on both concentration and exposure duration. This study, therefore, highlights the importance of incorporating long-term 3D hepatic in vitro models and transcriptomic endpoints into PFAS risk assessment and suggests that conventional short-term assays may underestimate the biological impact of sustained low-dose exposure. Key message (Impact of the study): This study provides systematic comparisons of short term (4 days) versus longer term (4 weeks), environmentally relevant GenX exposure in monocellular HepG2/C3A hepatic spheroids, revealing non-monotonic, time-dependent changes in mRNA levels encoding cellular components of lipid metabolism-related pathways with potential implications for appropriate dose and time exposure parameters for use in New Approach Methods to be applied in risk assessment.

papers.abstract_en: Human malaria infections begin with the injection of Plasmodium sporozoites via mosquito saliva. Whole sporozoite immunizations have been used as a model to study immune responses to malaria parasites, having culminated in circumsporozoite protein (CSP)-targeting vaccines and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). However, antibody responses targeting non-CSP antigens on the sporozoite surface remain poorly characterized. Here, we isolated single B cells from a human volunteer immunized by Plasmodium falciparum-infected mosquito bites, who had acquired non-CSP-specific antibodies that recognize sporozoites. We identified two mAbs that recognize the surface of P. falciparum sporozoites, but do not bind to CSP. Using immunoprecipitation followed by mass-spectrometry, we found that the target of these mAbs is not a P. falciparum protein but the mosquito salivary protein SG1L3. We observed that recombinant SG1L3 binds to P. falciparum sporozoites. However, the SG1L3-specific mAbs and SG1L3-specific polyclonal antibodies from this volunteer, as well as polyclonal antibodies raised against recombinant SG1L3 in rabbits, fail to block liver stage infection in vitro, making this an unlikely target for functional antibodies. We observed that inhabitants from an area with intense Anopheles exposure in Burkina Faso can have antibodies against SG1L3, and that antibody titers increase with age. In conclusion, we identified the first human mAbs against a mosquito saliva protein that binds to the surface of sporozoites. Future work should assess whether naturally acquired antibodies against this protein may be used as a serological marker of mosquito exposure.

papers.abstract_en: Polysaccharides, as structurally diverse and biologically versatile natural macromolecules, have long been recognized for their indispensable roles in immune regulation, intercellular communication, and tissue architecture. Their intrinsic biocompatibility, biodegradability, and chemical modifiability position them at the interface between small-molecule drugs, biologics, and functional biomaterials. This review provides a systematic overview of the biological characteristics, historical evolution, and clinical applications of polysaccharide-based drugs, with an emphasis on marketed products and advanced clinical candidates. We critically discuss recent progress in polysaccharide-based delivery platforms, including nanoparticles, hydrogels, and polysaccharide-drug conjugates, highlighting how molecular design-such as molecular weight control, glycosidic linkage configuration, and functional group substitution-governs pharmacological activity and targeting performance. Particular attention is given to antitumor applications, where natural and chemically modified polysaccharides (e.g., selenized, phosphorylated, and sulfated derivatives) exert multitarget effects through cell cycle arrest, apoptosis induction, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and immunomodulation. Despite significant advances, challenges related to structural heterogeneity, batch-to-batch variability, and incomplete structure-activity relationship elucidation continue to hinder clinical translation. By integrating structural precision with mechanistic clarity, polysaccharide-based drugs are poised to evolve from supportive agents into rationally designed, next-generation therapeutic platforms.

papers.abstract_en: Gliomas are the most common and highly harmful primary central nervous system tumors. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) has been proposed as a promising therapeutic strategy for glioma by specifically silencing target gene expression. However, the instability of siRNA and its poor permeability across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and blood-brain tumor barrier (BBTB) have significantly limited its clinical application. Therefore, appropriate delivery systems are urgently required to enhance the stability and targeting efficiency of siRNA. Nano-delivery systems, due to advantages such as protecting siRNA from being degraded by enzymes, increasing the rate of drug entry into the brain, and enabling targeted delivery, have become an effective means to solve the problem of siRNA treatment for glioma. This review outlines the design strategies, types, and application progress of siRNA nano-delivery systems for glioma treatment. It focuses on how biological macromolecule-based, polymer-based, lipid-based, inorganic, and biomimetic systems overcome in vivo delivery barriers through their material properties and functional modifications. The review also covers the mechanisms by which siRNA inhibits glioma, the strategies carriers use to cross the BBB, and combination therapy approaches. It then discusses the current challenges in this field and the prospects for clinical translation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Different socioeconomic and racial groups experience different environmental and health burdens across the United States, including for asthma. RESULTS: Cumulative exposures across lags 0-3 days were significantly associated with increased odds of asthma hospitalization for PM2.5 (OR = 1.079; 95% confidence interval = [1.052, 1.107]), O3 (1.082 [1.050, 1.116]), and NO2 (1.071 [1.034, 1.111]). Race-effect modification was not significant. Despite this, significant lag-specific patterns differed by race, with associations observed at lags 1-2 among Black children and at lag 3 among White children. In multipollutant models, associations were attenuated for O3 and NO2, while PM2.5 remained positively associated with asthma hospitalizations. CONCLUSIONS: Short-term increases in air pollution exposures are associated with an increased risk of hospitalizations for asthma among young populations in Louisiana. Given cumulative associations were similar across subgroups, the higher burden among Black children potentially highlights persistent exposure disparities. Reducing air pollution exposure may improve pediatric respiratory health.

CONCLUSION: This undercounting may limit resources for individuals with mental health-related disabilities. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterize pleuroparenchymal abnormalities identified on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) in cancer patients investigated for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE) and to compare imaging findings between patients with and without confirmed PE. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 113 consecutive cancer patients who underwent CTPA for suspected acute PE between January 2022 and January 2026. Radiology reports and electronic medical records were reviewed for demographic data, malignancy type and stage, PE-related imaging characteristics, and pleural and pulmonary parenchymal abnormalities. Imaging findings were compared between PE-positive and PE-negative groups. An exploratory multivariable model with a restricted set of imaging predictors was constructed to limit overfitting, with correction for multiple comparisons and bootstrap-based internal validation. Exploratory subgroup analyses by malignancy type and disease burden were also performed. RESULTS: PE was confirmed in 32 patients (28.3%). The median age was 59 years (IQR, 51-65), and 42.5% were female. The highest PE prevalence was observed in gastrointestinal, gynecologic, and thoracic malignancies. At nominal testing, infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity was more frequent in PE-positive patients (12.5% vs. 1.2%; OR, 11.43; p = 0.022), whereas ground-glass opacity (15.6% vs. 35.8%; OR, 0.33; p = 0.041) and interstitial/septal change (3.1% vs. 25.9%; OR, 0.09; p = 0.007) were less frequent. None remained statistically significant after false-discovery-rate correction (q = 0.133, 0.166, and 0.082, respectively). The parsimonious model had an apparent AUROC of 0.707 and an optimism-adjusted AUROC of 0.699, with acceptable grouped calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.522). No exploratory cancer-subgroup comparison met q < 0.05. CONCLUSIONS: Pleuroparenchymal abnormalities are highly prevalent in cancer patients undergoing CTPA for suspected PE; however, most findings are nonspecific. Infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity generated the strongest exploratory PE-associated signal, but no individual imaging comparison survived multiplicity correction and model estimates remained imprecise. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits variable treatment response and patients shown a median survival of 15 months. A major challenge lies in the difficulty of reliably assessing treatment response at an early stage, as it can usually only be evaluated on anatomical MRI performed up to three months after the start of treatment, when early interpretation may be complicated by the risk of pseudoprogression. Accurately predicting short-term and long-term survivors before radiotherapy and chemotherapy is therefore crucial. The objective of this study is to develop an AI model designed to predict survival outcomes based exclusively on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data. MATERIAL AND METHODS: A total of 1,575 retrospective T1-Gd brain images were obtained from 175 patients treated for GBM between 2018 and 2023. A ResNet-51Q model pretrained on ImageNet was fine-tuned on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI using transfer learning. To incorporate clinical data, deep hybrid learning (DHL) models were trained. RESULTS: At patient-level, the AI model achieved 81.08% (CI 95%: 67.57-91.89), 68.42% (CI 95%: 47.06-88.89) and 94.44% (CI 95%: 81.82-1.00) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively, for the classification of short-term and long-term survivors using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI. At patient-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.92- 97.44), 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.68-96.97), and 93.59% (CI 95%: 88.03-98.41) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison at slice-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 81.77% (CI 95%: 70.66-91.45), 81.77% (CI 95%: 71.07-91.33), and 90.88% (CI 95%: 85.25-95.74) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison the DHL model with clinical data achieved an accuracy of 84.62% (CI 95%: 71.79-94.87), a sensitivity of 84.62% (CI 95%: 72.54-95.24) and a specificity of 92.31% (CI 95%: 86.07-97.53) and 76.32% (CI 95%: 63.16-89.47), 76.11% (CI 95%: 61.63-88.75) and 92.06% (CI 95%: 87.51-96.23) for four overall survival classification. For multiclass tasks, metrics were calculated using a macro-averaged approach. CONCLUSION: The combination of pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data using the DHL model for early survival prediction; however, adding clinical variables yielded comparable prognostic performance rather than a demonstrable enhancement over imaging features alone. The use of AI models to predict survival outcome in GBM from pre-chemoradiotherapy data may support pre-chemoradiotherapy prognostic stratification.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Caregiver involvement in cognitively stimulating play is critical for children’s early development. Nevertheless, the role of fathers remains underexplored, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. This study examines the role of father involvement for developmental outcomes of sons and daughters under age 3 in rural Chinese households. METHODS: In July 2024, we surveyed a randomly selected sample of 6–24 months old and their caregivers (n=592) in an east coast province in China. Children’s cognition, language and motor development was measured using the Third Edition of the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development (Bayley-III). Father and primary caregiver involvement was assessed with the play activities scale, family care indicators. Given that most fathers (96.1%) in the study sample are non-primary caregivers, while mothers (72.0%) and grandmothers (22.8%) hold most primary caregiving roles, the study focuses on non-primary caregiving fathers. Multivariate linear regression models were used to assess relationships of Bayley-III scores with father and primary caregiver involvement. RESULTS: Involvement of non-primary caregiving fathers is low (ie, less than half the level of primary caregiver involvement). Less than 20% of fathers frequently tell stories or read books to their children. Children with more involved fathers (ie, above-median engagement in play activities) have, on average, Bayley-III composite cognitive, language and motor scores that are 5.1, 7.5 and 3.6 points higher than children with less involved fathers (ps<0.05). The results also provide suggestive evidence that father and primary-caregiver involvement each contribute to early language development, with their contributions accumulating when both are involved. Finally, contrary to traditional son preferences, fathers are found to engage more attentively with daughters, potentially as a result of changing times and cultural mores. CONCLUSIONS: Encouraging father involvement may serve as a promising approach to support young children in reaching developmental potential in rural China. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ISRCTN13421990.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: There is growing interest in virtual care provision to improve patient access to quality care, and while utilisation of virtual care services has increased, an evaluation of this modality of care is lacking. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate perceptions of a variety of virtual care services offered to children across Ontario throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: This perception-based evaluation included a cross-sectional study design guided by the Quintuple Aim Framework focused on population health, user experience, provider experience, cost and equity. Data were collected from 44 organisations that provided virtual care to children, 194 service providers with various specialties and 909 parents/caregivers of children who have received virtual care in Ontario. Participants completed unique online questionnaires. RESULTS: The services provided to children that were reportedly most compatible with a virtual setting, regardless of the participant type, included speech-language pathology, therapy and social work services. The services least compatible with a virtual setting were physiotherapy and autism services. While modifications are required, perceived quality of care is equal to somewhat reduced in a virtual setting, and virtual care is more accessible and circumvents barriers to in-person care. Consequently, a targeted hybrid approach is the preferred future for the provision of care to children in Ontario. CONCLUSIONS: Virtual care for children is not one size fits all. A targeted approach to providing care virtually, informed by this report, could optimise the allocation of virtual care resources to ensure its provision remains equitable and cost effective.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Prenatal phthalate exposure has been associated with allergic outcomes; however, evidence linking it to childhood asthma remains inconsistent. Using data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study (JECS), we examined the association between prenatal phthalate exposure measured during the first and second/third trimesters and current asthma in early childhood. METHODS: Among 9,707 mother-child pairs with urinary phthalate measurements in both the first and second/third trimesters, 8,554, 8,048, and 7,722 singleton children with available asthma data were analyzed at ages 2, 4, and 6 years, respectively. Current asthma was defined as wheezing in the past 12 months together with caregiver-reported physician-diagnosed asthma during that period (or ongoing asthma treatment). In the primary analyses, first-trimester, second/third-trimester, and average concentrations were analyzed using logistic regression adjusted for maternal allergy or asthma history, smoking, education, household income, parity, and recruitment center, with multiple imputation and false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Additional analyses included sex stratification, generalized estimating equations, mutually adjusted trimester-specific models, alternative asthma definitions, and quantile g-computation. RESULTS: Current asthma prevalence was 6.4, 5.8, and 4.4% at 2, 4, and 6 years, respectively. In the primary analyses, no associations remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Similarly, generalized estimating equation and quantile g-computation analyses showed no significant overall associations after FDR correction. In additional analyses after FDR correction, the average monomethyl phthalate (MMP) concentration was positively associated with International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC)-defined asthma at age 2, while first-trimester and average MMP concentrations were positively associated with later-confirmed age-2 asthma. These findings were not consistently observed across ages or analytic approaches. CONCLUSION: Prenatal phthalate exposure was not consistently associated with current asthma in early childhood in this large Japanese birth cohort. Although certain MMP associations emerged in secondary and sensitivity analyses, the overall pattern of findings did not support a robust association.

papers.abstract_en: Circadian disruption, notably induced by light at night (LAN), is increasingly recognized as a modulator of systemic immune function; however, its high-resolution spatiotemporal impact and relevance to cancer immunotherapy remain poorly defined. Here, we constructed a spatiotemporal single-cell transcriptomic atlas of murine lymph nodes, peripheral blood, and spleen across circadian time points to dissect the immunological consequences of LAN exposure. We observed that LAN exposure was associated with profound, tissue-specific transcriptional remodeling of the adaptive immune system. Specifically, B cells exhibited suppressed circadian clock programs and impaired homing and retention signatures. Concurrently, CD8+ T cells exhibited transcriptional profiles consistent with an aberrantly activated, late-effector state, a transition accompanied by altered intercellular MHC-I communication. To evaluate the translational relevance of these transcriptomic shifts, we developed a computational LAN Immune Dyssynchrony Score (LAN-IDS) and projected these murine-derived signatures onto human cancer cohorts. In human melanoma sentinel lymph nodes, the LAN-associated CD8+ T cell trajectory exhibited strong directional concordance with advanced (Stage III) disease. Crucially, interrogating these signatures within a clinical melanoma cohort revealed that the aberrantly activated CD8+ T cell program is significantly elevated in patients with primary resistance to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. Collectively, our cross-species computational analysis identifies a spatiotemporal adaptive immune dyssynchrony signature. These findings identify specific lymphocyte transcriptional states that may serve as candidate correlates of tumor progression and immunotherapy non-response.

papers.abstract_en: STUDY OBJECTIVES: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality, but the relative contributions of OSA-specific parameters versus classical cardiometabolic risk factors remain poorly defined. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 4,368 consecutive adults referred for diagnostic polysomnography at a tertiary sleep center and followed for up to 20 years. The primary outcome was cause-specific cardiovascular mortality ascertained by national death registry linkage. Analyses integrated cause-specific Cox regression, Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models, and a random survival forest (RSF) competing-risk model (1000 trees; 70/30 train-test split). Gower-distance-based hierarchical clustering of RSF-predicted cumulative incidence identified patient phenotypes. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 8.6 years (interquartile range 6.7-12.5), 335 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Heart failure (30.4%), chronic ischemic heart disease (14.0%), and acute myocardial infarction (11.6%) were the leading causes. Independent predictors were age (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.10, per year), male sex (1.68, 1.29-2.18), active smoking (1.68, 1.30-2.15), hypertension (1.73, 1.29-2.33), atrial fibrillation (2.16, 1.56-2.98), prior myocardial infarction (1.71, 1.25-2.35), and diabetes (1.37, 1.06-1.76). Nocturnal desaturation lost significance after multivariable adjustment. Among patients with an apnea-hypopnea index ≥15 events/h, a good continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) response was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (0.72, 0.55-0.96). The RSF C-index was 0.80. Six phenotypes showed cardiovascular mortality of 2.9% to 14.4%. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular mortality in OSA was driven predominantly by classical cardiometabolic risk factors rather than by nocturnal hypoxemic burden or CPAP response. Comorbidity-targeted prevention should be prioritized, and phenotype-aware stratification may identify subgroups warranting intensified cardiovascular surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: T-cell function is regulated by immunometabolism, and lysosomes are signaling hubs. CD68 (LAMP4), traditionally regarded as a monocyte/macrophage marker, has been largely neglected in T cell biology. We aimed to assess the link between CD68 expression in T cells and anti-PD-1 response in lung cancer, and its potential as an early dynamic biomarker in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells. METHODS: We analyzed transcriptomic (GSE126044, GSE135222, GSE166449) and single-cell (GSE207422) data from anti-PD-1-treated lung cancer cohorts to identify lysosome related pathways and key genes, validated with peripheral blood CD8+ T cell data (GSE111414). Prospectively, we enrolled lung cancer patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, collecting peripheral blood at baseline and week 3. Flow cytometry measured CD68 in CD8+ T cells and subsets, assessing association with response, progression-free survival (PFS), and functional markers (granzyme B, perforin, Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, IL-1β). RESULTS: Responders showed enrichment of lysosome pathways and upregulation of 8 lysosome related genes including CD68, positively correlated with monocyte and T cell infiltration. Single-cell data linked CD68 expression in T cell to favorable response. After one cycle, the proportion of CD8+CD68+ T cells was lower in non-responders (P<0.05), with AUC 0.803 (P=0.044) and cutoff 1.015%, stratifying PFS (P=0.0225). CD68 was highest in naïve T cells at baseline, but decreased across subsets after treatment in non-responders (all P<0.01). Functionally, compared with CD8+CD68- T cells, CD8+CD68+ T cells exhibited lower expression of granzyme B and perforin but higher expression of Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, and IL-1β (all P<0.001), suggesting a CD8+ T cell state characterized by lower cytotoxicity and enhanced proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, accompanied by a tissue residency associated phenotype. CONCLUSION: CD8+CD68+ T cells exhibit lower cytotoxicity but greater proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, together with a tissue residency associated phenotype, suggesting a precursor-like state. Low CD68 expression in tumor-infiltrating T cells and the post-treatment reduction of CD68 expression in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells are associated with resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer. These findings suggest that CD8+CD68+ T cells may serve as a potential early dynamic immune biomarker for monitoring and assessing response to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer.

papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a severe autoimmune inflammatory disease for which reliable biomarkers of disease activity are lacking. Meteorin-like protein (Metrnl) has not been investigated in NMOSD; this study assessed its clinical significance in NMOSD patients. METHODS: Serum Metrnl, interleukin (IL)-6, and IL-17A levels were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in 50 patients with NMOSD and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) and correlated with clinical and laboratory data. Metrnl levels were also remeasured in 30 patients before and after high-dose methylprednisolone therapy, together with derived inflammatory indices. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was applied within prespecified test families, with a sensitivity power analysis. Metrnl alone and a combined multimarker logistic regression model were evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, DeLong tests, bootstrap validation, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Serum Metrnl levels were higher in NMOSD patients than in HCs and were greater in those with mild disability than in those with moderate-to-severe disability (both p < 0.001); the increase in patients with gadolinium-enhancing lesions was nominal (p = 0.034, q = 0.068). After FDR correction, serum Metrnl levels correlated negatively with IL-6, IL-17A, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score (all q < 0.05), but not with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). Metrnl alone distinguished NMOSD patients from HCs (area under the curve [AUC] 0.752), whereas a combined model of Metrnl, IL-6, IL-17A, and hs-CRP performed markedly better (AUC 0.933; DeLong p < 0.001), increasing specificity from 53.3% to 80.0% at 100% sensitivity. After methylprednisolone therapy, Metrnl, IL-6, and IL-17A levels decreased (p < 0.001) along with clinical improvement, whereas NLR, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and SII remained unchanged; the decrease in Metrnl levels (median -25.5%) was the largest and was uncorrelated with changes in other biomarkers. CONCLUSIONS: Serum Metrnl levels were elevated in patients with NMOSD, inversely related to disease severity and inflammatory biomarkers, and decreased after immunotherapy, supporting it as a dynamic biomarker of disease activity and a component of a multimarker diagnostic panel. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and exploratory subgroup findings require external validation.

papers.title_zh: GlycoRNA-related cellular program scoring identifies Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments for glycoRNA validation.
papers.title_en: GlycoRNA-related cellular program scoring identifies Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments for glycoRNA validation.
papers.authors: Kong M, Guan X, Jing Y, Xie Z, Zhao X, Huang S, Yu Y, Zhang C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Cardiology, The Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, Luzhou, Sichuan, China.
papers.results: BACKGROUND: Glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) represent a recently recognized connection between RNA biology and cell-surface glycobiology. However, whether glycoRNA-related processes are relevant to human tumors remains unc…
papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) represent a recently recognized connection between RNA biology and cell-surface glycobiology. However, whether glycoRNA-related processes are relevant to human tumors remains unclear, partly because direct glycoRNA measurements are not yet available across large cancer cohorts. We therefore used transcriptomic data to identify tumor settings in which glycoRNA-related programs may be most suitable for further experimental validation. METHODS: We curated a glycoRNA-focused literature evidence base and manually reviewed the top extracted relations to define gene modules related to RNA identity, N-glycan and sialylation pathways, RNA trafficking, and lectin/Siglec recognition. The glycoRNA-related cellular program score is an expression-based composite score representing coordinated glycoRNA-related cellular programs, including RNA processing, glycan biosynthesis, trafficking, and lectin/Siglec recognition. It is designed to prioritize tumor contexts for experimental glycoRNA validation. The score was applied to 9,186 TCGA tumors from 32 cancer types and analyzed together with clinical variables, leukocyte fraction, immune signatures, Siglec/checkpoint/myeloid-axis scores, and non-overlapping sensitivity models. Glioblastoma single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets were used for additional context-level validation. RESULTS: Higher glycoRNA-related cellular program scores were observed in several tumor types, including stomach adenocarcinoma, glioblastoma, lung adenocarcinoma, esophageal carcinoma, mesothelioma, pancreatic adenocarcinoma, breast cancer, and lung squamous carcinoma. Survival analyses did not show robust FDR-significant associations after adjustment for age, sex, stage, and tumor type, suggesting that the score should not be interpreted as a general prognostic biomarker. In sensitivity analyses that removed immune and Siglec-related genes from the predictor, the score remained associated with Siglec-decoder, myeloid, checkpoint, and integrated niche features after adjustment for leukocyte fraction and cancer-type effects. Within-cancer meta-analysis supported these associations across cancer types, although effect sizes varied. In glioblastoma, higher scores were found in tumor, myeloid, mesenchymal, and niche-associated compartments in single-cell and spatial analyses. CONCLUSIONS: This study presents an expression-based map of glycoRNA-related cellular program across human cancers. The results suggest that glycoRNA-related transcriptional programs tend to occur in immune- and myeloid-enriched tumor microenvironments, particularly those involving Siglec-associated features. These findings prioritize tumor contexts for biochemical, imaging, spatial, and perturbation-based glycoRNA validation.

papers.title_zh: TRACER：响应保护的跨域对齐框架用于细胞系到患者肿瘤的药物反应模型迁移，其药物反应预测相关性未优于仅响应基线
papers.title_en: TRACER: response-protected cross-domain alignment of cancer pharmacogenomic models with patient tumors.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Wang Q, Wang G, Wang G, Zhao Y
papers.affiliation_highlight: College of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, Northeast Forestry University, No.
papers.results: ModelID-disjoint、seen-drug 划分下，TRACER-Full 在按药物 z 标准化的测试对上全局 Pearson 相关为 0.5125 ± 0.0192，Response-only 为 0.5179 ± 0.0193，平均差 −0.0054；在排除对齐的 TCGA 审计样本中，致癌 Hallmark 邻居一致性平均提高 0.1162 ± 0.0210；患者层面按 source-validation 定义的药物划分与均匀性稳定分析支持 BRCA 四个、UCEC 四个、SARC 两个预测药理反应亚型（PRS）
papers.authors_conclusion: TRACER 为保持响应的跨域对齐提供了一个可解释、可审计的框架，并生成可供后续功能验证的患者药物基因组学假设
papers.ai_note: 主要预测指标为阴性且被淡化：TRACER-Full 的全局 Pearson 相关（0.5125）低于不含对齐的 Response-only 基线（0.5179），摘要仅给出点估计差值 −0.0054，未报告该差值的 95%CI 或 P 值，无法判断是否等效或劣于基线；作者随即将叙述重心转向邻居一致性提升（0.1162）与 PRS 分型，而后者属无标签聚类稳定性结果，不构成外部或功能验证。PRS 数目依赖 source-validation 定义的药物划分，划分敏感性未在摘要中报告。全部结果为回顾性内部审计，缺乏独立队列、前瞻验证与湿实验确认；各数据集样本量与 PRS 稳定性具体统计量缺失，信息不足

pico.p: 体外筛选细胞系药物反应数据（ModelID-disjoint、seen-drug 划分）与 TCGA 患者肿瘤样本审计集；患者层面分析涉及乳腺浸润癌（BRCA）、子宫体子宫内膜癌（UCEC）与肉瘤（SARC）。摘要未报告各数据集样本量
pico.ic: 干预：TRACER（TRACER-Full，监督式药物反应预测＋生物条件约束的邻居对齐＋响应保护的梯度调控）。对照：Response-only（不含辅助对齐的响应优化基线）；另设 alignment-excluded 审计与 PRS-construction-excluded 药物的内部一致性分析

papers.reason: 为跨域药物反应预测提供了带阴性主要结果的对照基线（Response-only 已经优于复杂对齐方案），可用于评估后续药物基因组学迁移方法的增益是否真实；其结果仅为假设生成，对胸部肿瘤当前的用药或手术决策无直接影响
papers.abstract_en: Pharmacogenomics integrates tumor molecular features with drug responses to support precision oncology, but biological domain shifts and optimization conflicts hinder transfer from screened cell lines to unlabeled patient tumors. We developed TRACER (Transfer of Response Across domains via Conflict-aware End-to-end Regulation), an end-to-end framework combining supervised drug-response prediction, biologically conditioned neighbor alignment and response-protected gradient regulation. By projecting only conflicting components of the auxiliary alignment gradient, TRACER preserves the response-optimization direction learned from experimental labels. Across ModelID-disjoint, seen-drug splits, TRACER-Full achieved a global Pearson correlation of 0.5125 $\pm $ 0.0192 on per-drug z-standardized test pairs, compared with 0.5179 $\pm $ 0.0193 for Response-only, a mean difference of $-0.0054$. Mean oncogenic Hallmark neighbor consistency increased by $0.1162 \pm 0.0210$ in alignment-excluded The Cancer Genome Atlas audit samples. At the patient level, a source-validation-defined drug partition and uniform stability analysis supported four predicted pharmacological response subtypes (PRSs) in breast invasive carcinoma (BRCA), four in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) and two in sarcoma (SARC). PRS-construction-excluded drugs characterized distinct predicted mechanism-level profiles, and pan-cancer indication recovery provided a lineage-aware internal consistency assessment of the patient rankings. TRACER provides an interpretable and auditable framework for response-preserving cross-domain alignment and it generates patient pharmacogenomic hypotheses for subsequent functional validation.

papers.authors: Wagner J, Rajan D, Field SF, Betteridge E, Bellis K, Knoll M, Ng D, Teixeira D et al.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sequencing respiratory virus genomes is essential for public health surveillance and research. Although shotgun metagenomics is pathogen agnostic, its sensitivity is limited by abundant off-target host nucleic acids. Hybridization bait capture overcomes this limitation by selectively enriching viral sequences prior to sequencing. METHODS: We evaluated three respiratory viral bait capture workflows (veSEQ, RVI-seq, and Illumina) to compare their performance and assess their suitability for scalable respiratory virus sequencing. Synthetic RNA controls and clinical samples containing SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, human parainfluenza virus, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were analysed. RESULTS: All three workflows demonstrated high efficiency, reproducibility and broadly comparable performance across respiratory viruses. Complete viral genomes were consistently recovered from samples containing 10,000 viral copies, while viral reads remained detectable at substantially lower viral loads, including approximately 100 copies. Workflow optimisation reduced reagent costs and enabled laboratory automation without compromising sequencing sensitivity. CONCLUSION: Hybridization bait capture provides an effective and scalable approach for respiratory virus genome sequencing. Cost reductions and automation can be implemented without compromising performance, supporting its use in routine genomic surveillance and public health preparedness.

papers.abstract_en: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a major cause of low back pain, driven largely by nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence under chronic hypoxia and nutrient stress. Serine metabolism regulates senescence, but its role in IVDD remains unclear. Here, transcriptomic profiling reveals that the glycine-serine-threonine pathway is downregulated in senescent NPCs, with marked reduction of the serine synthesis rate limiting enzyme PHGDH. This is confirmed by single cell RNA sequencing of human discs, aged rat tissues, and degenerated human samples, accompanied by decreased intracellular serine. PHGDH silencing or serine deprivation inhibits NPC proliferation, induces senescence, and suppresses matrix anabolism. Mechanistically, PHGDH deficiency lowers α ketoglutarate, impairing histone demethylation and increasing H3K27me3 occupancy at the Rap1b promoter, which silences Rap1b and activates mTORC1, thereby blocking autophagic flux. Additionally, serine starvation depletes glutathione, elevates ROS, and promotes apoptosis. In vivo, AAV mediated PHGDH overexpression alleviates puncture induced IVDD, while a serine deficient diet exacerbates degeneration. Collectively, we uncover a PHGDH/Rap1b/mTORC1/autophagy cascade linking serine deprivation to NPC senescence, and propose that restoring PHGDH or serine availability may be a viable strategy to combat age related disc degeneration.

papers.authors: Qiu Y, Sun K, Yu Y, Hou H, Wu R, Lu Q, Zhao M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Hospital for Skin Diseases, Institute of Dermatology, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical Colle…

papers.abstract_en: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)-SE regulating IL1A, IL1B, and IL36G transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE-centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

papers.abstract_en: The tumor microenvironment is a critical factor in understanding cancer progression and metastasis. In this context, isolating tumor interstitial fluid (TIF) is a powerful tool for detecting cancer biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In our study, we conducted a proteomic analysis of TIFs from metastatic lung nodules using a murine model. The TIFs from these lungs were enriched with actin-binding proteins, among other molecules. Notably, we identified Scinderin (Scin), an actin-binding protein secreted by tumor cells. Knockdown of Scin resulted in a significant decrease in the number and size of lung nodules, as well as a reduction, albeit to a lesser extent, in disseminated tumor cells (DTCs). Furthermore, silencing Scin inhibited cell and tumor growth in different cancer cell lines. In human tumors, Scin was detected in the tumor interstitial fluid (TIF) of endometrial cancer patients. Scin was expressed abundantly in serous endometrial carcinomas and in the secretory endometrium. Remarkably, a paired analysis using an endometrial cancer tissue-array revealed increased Scin expression in metastatic samples compared to their corresponding primary tumors. In addition, a retrospective study revealed that levels of Scin in plasma were significantly elevated in patients who developed metastases. These findings suggest that Scin plays a significant role in the metastatic process and may serve as a promising biomarker for tumor aggressiveness and metastatic potential.

papers.abstract_en: Despite their significance, the genetic and molecular bases of neurodevelopmental disorders remain poorly understood. In this study, using human brain organoids and mouse models, we show that loss of NDE1, a gene closely associated with microcephaly, disrupts progenitor identity, prolongs mitosis, and alters regional patterning in the forebrain. NDE1 knockout leads to a caudal identity shift of neural progenitor cells in the organoids and mouse brains, coinciding with aberrant ERK signaling. Notably, downstream activation of the ERK pathway restored rostral PAX6 expression in human brain organoids. Parallel analyses of Nde1 knockout mice confirmed disrupted regional patterning of the forebrain. Together, our data establish NDE1 as a critical regulator of early human brain regionalization and elucidate molecular mechanisms underlying the structural abnormalities observed in NDE1-associated microcephaly.

papers.abstract_en: Th2 cells play a central role in orchestrating type 2 immune responses by producing type 2 cytokines including IL-4 and IL-13. The master transcription factor GATA3 is essential but not sufficient for type 2 cytokine production. To better define other transcription factors that regulate type 2 cytokine expression, we performed a CRISPR-Cas9 screen after preparing a retroviral library expressing sgRNAs targeting 2,394 mouse transcription factors and cofactors. The screen revealed core-binding factor beta (Cbfβ) as a specific inducer of IL-13 that simultaneously inhibited IL-4 expression. The effect of Cbfβ on IL-13 production was confirmed both in vitro and in vivo and was independent of GATA3 induction. Mechanistically, Cbfβ induced chromatin accessibility at the HS-2 site within the Il13 promoter where the Cbfβ/Runx complex bound. Hi-TrAC analysis indicated that DNA looping between HS-2 and other enhancers was reduced upon Cbfβ deletion. Overall, our results indicate that Cbfβ directly regulates IL-13 expression by binding the Il13 promoter via the Cbfβ/Runx complex and promoting enhancer-promoter interactions that facilitate Il13 transcription.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiac lymphatics regulate fluid homeostasis and immune cell clearance. The mechanisms underlying cardiac lymphatic vessel formation remain unclear. We perform spatial transcriptomics on the zebrafish heart at the single-cell level and investigate gene expression patterns in cardiac lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). adrenomedullin a (adma) is mainly expressed in the epicardium adjacent to cardiac lymphatics. adma mutants develop edema and dilated outflow tracts with mis-patterned and reduced lymphatics, while their ventricular lymphatics are dilated with fewer sprouts, increased lyve1b expression, and altered lymphatic subpopulation composition. Loss of ackr3a, which encodes an Adm decoy receptor, increases lymphatic sprouts. During heart regeneration, adma and ackr3a are expressed in epicardium-derived cells within the wound. Neutrophil clearance is reduced in adma mutants but increased in ackr3a mutants. Our findings uncover the heterogeneity of cardiac LECs and show that Adm and Ackr3 regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation in the zebrafish heart.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The revision of the WHO classification of CNS tumours now distinguishes grade 4 diffuse gliomas by their molecular features, but tailored treatment is yet to be standardised. Glioblastoma (isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH))-wildtype tumours harbouring an unmethylated O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase "(uMGMT)" promoter are inherently resistant to temozolomide (TMZ). However, no standardised treatment recommendations are available for grade 4 astrocytoma IDH-mutant. We previously demonstrated that administration of bortezomib (BTZ) 48 h prior to TMZ depletes MGMT protein and sensitizes uMGMT glioma cells to TMZ. Based on these findings, a phase IB/II trial was initiated to evaluate the safety and clinical activity of sequential BTZ and TMZ. This interim analysis aimed to determine a futility safeguard, identify molecular and pharmacodynamic determinants of treatment response and failure in the first 15 patients consecutively treated. METHODS: Adult patients with recurrent grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma or IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, uMGMT promoter, measurable disease, Karnofsky Performance Status ≥ 70, and disease progression ≥ 12 weeks after radiotherapy were enrolled. Patients received intravenous BTZ 1.3 mg/m² on days 1, 4, and 7 of each 28-day cycle, followed by oral TMZ 200 mg/m²/day for 5 consecutive days beginning on day 3. Targeted sequencing of glioma-associated genes and longitudinal plasma proteomic profiling using LC-MS/MS were performed before, during, and after treatment. RESULTS: Fifteen patients (median age 52 years) comprised 10 patients with IDH- wildtype glioblastoma and 5 patients with grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma. Disease control (partial response and stable disease) was observed in 4/10 (40%) IDH- wildtype glioblastoma patients, comprising one PR and three cases of SD. In contrast, all five patients with grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma experienced rapid progressive disease. Notably, non-responding IDH-wildtype glioblastomas and all IDH-mutant tumours harboured alterations affecting the CDKN2A/RB1-cell-cycle regulatory axis, including CDKN2A and/or RB1loss, with one IDH-mutant patient additionally harbouring PIK3CA gain. By comparison, responding IDH-wildtype glioblastomas were characterized by amplified EGFR, nuclear NF-κB (p65/RelA) activation, and absence of RB-pathway alterations. Longitudinal proteomic analyses demonstrated comparatively attenuated treatment-induced changes in proteins associated with invasion and extracellular matrix remodelling in responders, whereas proteins involved in damage clearance immune phenotype, platelet activation, aggregation, and degranulation were significantly altered during disease control. CONCLUSIONS: Sequential BTZ and TMZ therapy was feasible with manageable hematologic and non-hematologic toxicities and met prespecified interim futility criteria, supporting continued recruitment to the phase II study. Disease control was restricted to a molecularly defined subset of IDH- wildtype glioblastoma characterized by EGFR amplification and NF-κB activation. In contrast, universal treatment failure among grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytomas was associated with alterations of the CDKN2A/RB1 cell-cycle checkpoint pathway, suggesting that advanced molecular evolution and cell-cycle deregulation may override the survival advantage typically associated with IDH-mutant gliomas and limit the effectiveness of MGMT-targeted sensitization strategies. REGISTRY: ClinicalTrials.gov trial registration number: NCT03643549, date of registration: 2018-08-21.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: BTB domain containing 9 (BTBD9) is among the most reproducible genetic risk factors for sleep-related disorders, yet its molecular function in sleep regulation remains unclear. Here, we aimed to define the downstream substrate, core brain region, and molecular mechanism through which BTBD9 regulates sleep-wake homeostasis. METHODS: Population-scale genomic and brain expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) datasets were integrated to infer the direction of BTBD9-associated genetic risk in sleep-related traits. Basal forebrain-specific neuronal manipulation of Btbd9 was combined with electroencephalography/electromyography (EEG/EMG)-based sleep analysis and fiberphotomerty to define the relevant brain locus and functional output. Ubiquitinomics, protein interaction, ubiquitination, and enzymatic assays were used to identify BTBD9-regulated substrates and determine how BTBD9-dependent modification affects metabolic enzyme activity. Basal forebrain-specific genetic disruption, receptor pharmacology, and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-delivered interfering peptides were further applied to test pathway necessity and reversibility in vivo. RESULTS: human genetic analyses showed that BTBD9 variants associated with higher expression predicted a pro-arousal tendency. Consistently, neuron-specific deletion of Btbd9 in the mouse basal forebrain increased non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and extracellular adenosine levels. Mechanistically, IMPDH2, the rate-limiting enzyme in de novo purine biosynthesis, was identified as a substrate of the Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase 3 (CRL3)BTBD9 ubiquitin ligase. BTBD9-mediated ubiquitination at IMPDH2 lysine 195 (K195) relieved guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-dependent allosteric inhibition, thereby limiting adenosine accumulation and sleep pressure. Basal forebrain neuronal knockout of Impdh2 recapitulated the sleep-promoting effect of Btbd9 deletion, whereas adenosine A1 receptor (A1R) blockade attenuated this phenotype. AAV-delivered interfering peptides targeting the BTBD9-IMPDH2 interaction reduced IMPDH2 ubiquitination, elevated adenosine levels, increased NREM sleep, and rescued BTBD9 overexpression-induced abnormal wakefulness in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify a BTBD9-IMPDH2-adenosine pathway that links human genetic risk to basal forebrain control of sleep homeostasis. By defining BTBD9 as a molecular regulator of purine metabolism, this study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding and potentially targeting BTBD9-related sleep dysregulation.

papers.abstract_en: Electrical stimulation (ES) is widely acknowledged as an efficient means for enhancing bone repair. Despite the promising results of synergistic techniques that integrate conductive nanomaterials and ES in excitable tissues, their utilization in bone defect repair is yet inadequately investigated, given the inherent bioelectrical characteristics of bone tissue. In this work, a new osteogenic polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/pectin/MXene (Ti3C2Tx) (PPM) conductive composite hydrogel membrane is designed and comprehensively assessed for its efficacy in electrically enhanced bone regeneration. The PPM membrane with a durable threedimensional (3D) conductive network is formed by combining mechanically resilient, biocompatible PVA and bioactive pectin with highly conductive MXene nanosheets. PVA ensures mechanical integrity and structural stability, pectin with many functional groups promotes cell adhesion and osteogenic bioactivity, while the integration of MXene significantly enhances electrical conductivity, promoting cellular electrical signal transmission and modulating osteogenic cell activities. The PPM membrane has advantageous electrical, mechanical characteristics, and excellent in vitro cytocompatibility and improved osteogenic potential. In vivo experiments indicate that the PPM membrane markedly enhances new bone growth when subjected to ES. This study presents a synergistic approach utilizing a conductive hydrogel membrane and ES, providing a viable biomaterial platform for the repair of bone defects.

papers.abstract_en: To synergistically enhance the strength-ductility trade‑off and achieve uniform degradation in Fe-Zn alloys, heterostructured alloy microtubes were fabricated via layer‑by‑layer electrodeposition on a rotating soluble aluminum mandrel. Microstructural characterization revealed a columnar‑layered architecture with coherent interfacial bonding after annealing, free of delamination or defects. The heterostructured sample containing ten alternating soft layers (FZ10) exhibited an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 605 MPa and an elongation of about 17.3%, both superior to those of the single-layer alloy. The loading-unloading-reloading (LUR) experiments demonstrated pronounced hetero-deformation induced (HDI) strengthening and HDI strain-hardening effects, indicating the critical role of interfacial constraints in deformation coordination. Electrochemical and simulated body fluid (SBF) immersion tests showed that the heterostructure promoted faster and more uniform corrosion, with an average degradation rate of approximately 0.135 mm·y- 1 after 56 days, suppressing localized pitting. XPS and FTIR analyses identified the corrosion products as Fe/Zn oxides and Ca-P compounds, forming a bilayer degradation film with a dense inner layer and a loose outer layer. Additionally, heterostructured Fe-Zn alloy microtubes exhibited favorable cytocompatibility. These heterostructured microtubes integrate high strength, ductility, and controlled and uniform degradability, making them promising candidates for further development as biodegradable vascular stent materials.

papers.abstract_en: Xyloglucan, an immunomodulatory hemicellulose, shows potential for promoting chronic wound healing. However, tunable hydrogels composed solely of xyloglucan with a defined anti-inflammatory mechanism remain elusive. To address this, we developed a single-component, inherently bioactive oxidized xyloglucan (OXG) hydrogel that integrates anti-inflammatory functionality with extracellular matrix (ECM)-mimetic properties. The hydrogel forms autonomously via dynamic hemiacetal crosslinking between aldehyde and hydroxyl groups on the OXG backbone, eliminating the need for exogenous crosslinkers or drug loading. This strategy enables OXG to function both as an immunomodulator and as a supportive scaffold, exhibiting tissue adhesion, injectability, self-healing, and stability in physiological environments. In vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that the OXG hydrogel promotes M2 macrophage polarization and suppresses pro-inflammatory responses by activating the cAMP-PKA signaling pathway, leading to a metabolic shift and inflammation resolution without exogenous cytokines. These actions collectively accelerated diabetic wound closure, enhanced angiogenesis, and facilitated orderly tissue regeneration. This work established a drug-free hydrogel dressing with a well-defined anti-inflammatory mechanism by leveraging the inherent biological activity and self-gelling capability of a single polysaccharide, achieving active remodeling of the immune environment in chronic diabetic wounds. These findings position OXG as a promising natural anti-inflammatory biomaterial for tissue engineering and therapeutics.

papers.abstract_en: Electrical stimulation (ES) offers a robust approach to boost the efficacy of stem cell transplantation therapy for the treatment of neurological disorders. Notably, wireless technology blends convenience with the elimination of infection risk posed by wired connections, but the challenge lies in the integration of wireless-enabled stimulation materials and stem cell carriers. Here, we describe a flexible annular conductive dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid (HAD)/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/carbon nanotube‌ (CNT) hydrogel that acts as a secondary coil to realize wireless ES via electromagnetic induction, while also serving as a three-dimensional (3D) scaffold carrier for endogenous neural stem cells (NSCs). Established on the annular HAD/PVA/CNT hydrogel with high conductivity and good biocompatibility, wireless ES significantly enhances neuronal differentiation of NSCs. Furthermore, transplantation of the NSC-laden annular hydrogel into a traumatic brain injury (TBI) rat model modulates the behaviors of both exogenous and endogenous neural cells. The combined therapy of wireless ES and NSC transplantation promotes neuronal differentiation in both the injury zone and hippocampus in association with the PI3K-Akt pathway, reduces post-traumatic inflammatory responses, and effectively restores motor and memory functions in TBI rats. This study offers a promising therapeutic strategy of integrating wireless ES with stem cell transplantation therapy for brain injury repair.

papers.abstract_en: Despite considerable progress in cancer immunotherapy, the therapeutic efficacy of current cancer therapy continues to be hampered by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (ITME), which is characterized by acidification, hypoxia, elevated H2O2 levels, and aberrant angiogenesis. While transition metal-based nanomaterials hold great promise for modulating the ITME, their effectiveness is often constrained by insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, low immunogenicity, poor immune cell infiltration, and T-cell exhaustion. To address these issues, we developed a bimetallic Cu/Mn-doped nanoplatform, CMPTL, which further integrates acid-dissociable taurine and the angiogenesis inhibitor lenvatinib for malignant solid tumor therapy. This nanoplatform simultaneously triggers violent ROS and cuproptosis, leading to mitochondrial damage and the release of mitochondrial DNA. The subsequent activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, synergistically enhanced by Mn2+, initiates robust immune responses. Additionally, taurine helps alleviate T-cell exhaustion, while lenvatinib promotes tumor vessel normalization, leading to comprehensive remodeling of the TIME. Together, these multimodal mechanisms endow CMPTL with potent antitumor activity, positioning it as a promising candidate for cancer therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The cultures of human nasal epithelial cells (NECs) are good surrogate models for studying immune responses. Three-dimensional (3D) organoids have emerged as an alternative for nasal epithelium, serving as robust platforms for modeling respiratory viral infections. We aimed to generate human NEC organoids and to determine their cellular characteristics as an in vitro model for air-liquid interface (ALI) culture and influenza A virus (IAV) infection. METHODS: Primary human nasal mucosal tissues were obtained from healthy donors undergoing nasal surgery, and nasal epithelial cell (NEC) organoids were established using Matrigel-based three-dimensional culture. Differentiated NEC organoids and air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures were characterized by histology, immunostaining, electron microscopy, and quantitative real-time PCR, followed by influenza A virus (A/WS/33, H1N1) infection assays. In addition, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to analyze cellular heterogeneity and differentiation trajectories of NEC organoids. RESULTS: We successfully developed human NEC organoids with using a Matrigel-based 3D culture system that recapitulates the structural characteristics and cellular composition of the human nasal epithelium. Histological results, real-time PCR, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) revealed that the organoids consisted of seven different cell types and displayed a difference in the composition between the cells. The organoids displayed a much higher rate of basal progenitor cells whereas ciliated cells were less dominant. Unlike ALI cultures in which passage (P) 2 was the limit, the organoids exhibited successful and subsequent passages up to P5. Our data determined that NEC organoids are an adequate in vitro model for IAV infection and showed a sharp induction of mRNA levels for interferons (IFNs) and IFN-stimulated genes following IAV infection. CONCLUSIONS: This study's results demonstrate that human NEC organoids serve as a robust in vitro model, successfully recapitulating the biological characteristics of nasal epithelium, and could be an adequate tool for exploring distinct IFN-related innate immune responses following influenza infection.
