papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic inflammatory airway disease, characterised by dysregulated interactions between innate and adaptive immune cells. Although Th2-mediated inflammation predominates, persistent Th17-associated immune responses contribute to chronic airway inflammation implicated in the corticosteroid-insensitive disease state. Fluoxetine, a SSRI with immunomodulatory properties, was investigated to determine its effects on inflammation and Th17 response in experimental allergic airway disease. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Immunomodulatory effects of fluoxetine evaluated in exploratory in vitro assays. In vivo studies were performed in an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model of allergic asthma using oral fluoxetine at clinically relevant doses. Airway pathology, immunophenotypes, cytokine production, gene and protein expression were evaluated by histology, flow cytometry, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), confocal microscopy and ex vivo functional assays. Public transcriptomic datasets were integrated with target enrichment analyses, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations used to explore potential molecular interactions. KEY RESULTS: Fluoxetine reduced the inflammatory response in activated macrophages without noticeable cytotoxicity. In an allergic asthma model, fluoxetine attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, eosinophilia, IgE production and pulmonary macrophage activation, whilst reducing the accumulation of the phenotypically granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor like cell population along with diminished T-cell activation and reduced Th17 responses, reduced IL-17 production together with decreased expression and nuclear localisation of RORγt. Ex vivo studies confirmed inhibition of RORγt expression and IL-17 production in Th17 cells. Transcriptomic integration identified significant enrichment of Th17-associated inflammatory pathways, whereas molecular docking and molecular dynamics analyses supported RORγt as a plausible molecular target. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Fluoxetine attenuates experimental allergic airway inflammation through coordinated modulation of innate and adaptive immune responses, with suppression of the RORγt-IL-17 signalling axis emerging as a key mechanistic feature. These findings expand the immunopharmacological profile of fluoxetine and provide an experimental rationale for further investigating its therapeutic potential in Th17-associated airway inflammatory diseases and in experimental models that more closely recapitulate corticosteroid-resistant asthma.

papers.abstract_en: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) studies have traditionally relied on blood as the primary DNA source and manual workflows. As population-based genomics studies expand, minimally invasive and easily deployable biospecimen collection methods compatible with high-throughput automation are increasingly needed. In this pilot study, we established a real-world, end-to-end automated WGS workflow, encompassing robotic DNA extraction, library preparation, sequencing and quality control. We compared saliva- and blood-derived WGS across key analytical parameters, including performance at each step of the workflow, overall cost, and feasibility for future large-scale implementation. First, germline variant calls from saliva and blood samples showed high concordance, reaching 97% genome-wide and over 99% in high-confidence genomic regions. Second, key workflow metrics, including DNA quality and sequencing quality, were comparable between saliva and blood samples, while saliva samples had a lower per-sample cost. We compared three commercially available saliva collection kits and found that all achieved at least 95% genome-wide concordance with matched blood samples, with differences primarily driven by cost. Finally, automated saliva processing produced sequencing and short variant calling metrics broadly comparable to manual processing in a small paired comparison. Collectively, these results provide a practical and scalable solution for incorporating saliva into future large cohort sequencing studies. Larger and more diverse studies are needed to further validate the robustness and generalizability of this pilot study.

papers.abstract_en: Mercury is a persistent global pollutant, and methylmercury (MeHg) remains a major environmental health concern because human exposure continues through seafood consumption and severe contamination events. Although MeHg neurotoxicity has classically been linked to cerebellar and sensorimotor dysfunction, clinical and epidemiological studies have also reported psychiatric and behavioral disturbances, for which the underlying circuit pathology remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether subchronic MeHg exposure disrupts inhibitory control in forebrain circuits involved in emotional and behavioral regulation. Male mice were given 30 ppm MeHg in drinking water for up to 8 weeks, a high-dose paradigm designed to model severe subchronic MeHg intoxication and examine circuit-level neuropathology and behavior. MeHg exposure produced region-selective neuronal injury, characterized by increased TUNEL labeling and reduced NeuN-positive cells, in the anterior cingulate cortex, nucleus accumbens, mediodorsal thalamus, central amygdala, and basolateral amygdala. Across these regions, the inhibitory neuronal marker glutamate decarboxylase 65/67 (GAD65/67) was consistently reduced, whereas the excitatory presynaptic terminal markers vesicular glutamate transporter 1 and 2 (VGLUT1/2) were relatively preserved. c-Fos-positive cells showed an overall increasing trend across these regions, reaching statistical significance in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC); together, this pattern was consistent with a shift toward forebrain circuit disinhibition. Behaviorally, MeHg-exposed mice developed hyperactivity and stereotypic jumping behavior. Importantly, the GABAergic modulator chlormezanone reduced hyperactivity and abolished stereotypic jumping. Together, these findings support forebrain inhibitory dysfunction as a mechanistically relevant feature of MeHg neurotoxicity and suggest that impaired inhibitory control contributes to MeHg-induced psychomotor abnormalities. This study expands the neuropathological framework of MeHg toxicity beyond classical sensorimotor lesions and supports the inclusion of circuit-level neurobehavioral endpoints in hazard characterization of environmental neurotoxicants.

papers.abstract_en: Thallium (Tl) is a highly toxic metal, yet its bioaccumulation in marine organisms remains poorly understood. Reference concentration factors (CFs) recommended by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) imply substantial Tl bioaccumulation potential, whereas Tl concentrations in marine organisms are generally low. Here, we resolved this apparent discrepancy by characterizing Tl toxicokinetics in eleven marine species spanning macroalgae, mollusks, and crustaceans using stable-isotope tracing (203Tl). Across taxa, Tl was rapidly eliminated (ke = 0.33-3.67 d-1), resulting in low kinetic bioconcentration factors (BCFs: 16-336 L kg-1 dry weight and 0.51-68 L kg-1 wet weight). Interspecies variation in Tl accumulation was more strongly associated with uptake than with elimination. Dissolved uptake dominated bioaccumulation when particulate Tl was present, with little particulate contribution in most species with the tested SPM; oysters were an exception, showing enhanced accumulation and a particulate Tl assimilation efficiency of 33.5%. These results demonstrate that rapid elimination broadly limits Tl bioaccumulation across marine taxa and support re-evaluation of the high CFs currently used as reference values. Rapid turnover further indicates that tissue Tl concentrations primarily reflect recent exposure rather than long-term retention.

papers.abstract_en: Occupational exposure to pesticides has been increasingly associated with adverse health outcomes, potentially mediated by post-transcriptional mechanisms such as microRNA (miRNA) regulation. However, data on miRNA profiles in healthy exposed populations remain limited, particularly with respect to exposure duration. This study aimed to analyze miRNA expression profiles in occupationally exposed individuals according to exposure time and to elucidate underlying mechanisms and potential biomarkers. We conducted a cross-sectional study of occupationally exposed (n = 32) and non-exposed (n = 16) individuals. Differential expression analysis identified 14 miRNAs altered between groups (p < 0.01); stratification by exposure duration revealed 7 miRNAs altered in short-term exposure (5-20 years) and 16 miRNAs in long-term exposure (>30 years). Additionally, machine learning algorithms were applied to identify robust biomarker candidates. By intersecting multiple linear regression and machine learning outputs, we consistently identified miR-1255b-5p (AUC 0.861-0.768) and miR-433-5p (AUC 0.744-0.611) as potential biomarkers of overall exposure. Additionally, miR-620 (AUC 0.938-0.785) was associated with shorter exposure periods, while miR-1269a (AUC 1.000-0.820) and miR-519d-3p (AUC 0.812-0.719) were selected for long-term exposure. Significant correlations were found between specific miRNAs and quantified pesticide residues, notably a negative correlation between miR-1269a and imidacloprid metabolite (r = -0.53, p = 0.03) and positive correlations with carbofuran (r = 0.57, p = 0.02) and desdimethyldiuron (r = 0.57, p = 0.02). Our findings provide new evidence that occupational pesticide exposure is associated with specific alterations in circulating miRNA profiles. miRNA profiling has emerged as a promising tool for risk assessment, though longitudinal studies with larger cohorts are warranted to validate these biomarkers.

papers.abstract_en: Occupational exposure to 1-bromopropane (1-BP) has been linked to impairments in learning and memory; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely defined. Cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (CDK5), a critical regulator of neuronal function and synaptic plasticity, is aberrantly activated in multiple neurodegenerative conditions and toxin-induced neuronal injury. Here, we investigated whether CDK5 contributes to 1-BP-induced hippocampal neurotoxicity by promoting mitochondrial dysfunction. Using mouse and N2a cell models, we showed that 1-BP exposure triggered calpain-mediated proteolysis, increased p25 generation, and enhanced CDK5 activation in hippocampal neurons and N2a cells. CDK5 activation was accompanied by elevated Drp1 expression and phosphorylation, indicative of excessive mitochondrial fission and fragmentation. These mitochondrial abnormalities were associated with neuronal death, as evidenced by increased TUNEL-positive cells and upregulation of the necroptosis-related proteins RIPK1 and MLKL. Pharmacological inhibition of CDK5 with roscovitine markedly suppressed 1-BP-induced mitochondrial fission and neuronal necroptosisin N2a cells. Consistently, heterozygous Cdk5 haploinsufficiency mitigated mitochondrial structural and functional damage, reduced hippocampal neuronal loss, and improved learning and memory deficits in 1-BP-exposed mice. Together, these findings identify the CDK5/Drp1 axis as a critical mediator of 1-BP-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and hippocampal neuronal injury, providing mechanistic insight into the neurotoxicity of 1-BP.

papers.abstract_en: We describe here an efficient method for gene editing in mouse T cells, based on well-established, high-efficiency retroviral transduction protocols. Our platform allows analysis of mutant phenotypes in primary murine T cells in vitro and in vivo. This approach uses a single retroviral vector to simultaneously knockout an endogenous gene and ectopically express its mutant version. This knockout/re-expression vector can be used as the only plasmid to transduce Cas9-expressing T cells, or used together with a Cas9 retroviral vector to transduce T cells from any mouse strain. We validated the system for analysis of murine T cells by targeting key molecules in proximal T cell signaling, i.e. CD3γ and Zap70. We obtain high knockout and re-expression efficiencies in both Cas9-expressing and non-Cas9 T cells. Knockout efficiencies can be further improved by gRNA multiplexing. Endogenous proteins compete with their ectopically expressed mutants or tagged versions for cellular location, protein interactions and cellular functions. Here, we quantified the incorporation of CD3γ-GFP into surface T cell receptor (TCR) complexes. Our data shows that the knockout and re-expression platform improves integration of CD3γ-GFP into the TCR. Therefore, eliminating competition between endogenous and ectopic proteins benefits analyses of protein assemblies and signaling pathways in primary T cells. Furthermore, we validated advantages of our system for mutant analysis using wild-type and mutant Zap70s. Zap70 mutants deficient in TCR binding or kinase activity show their phenotypes only in the absence of endogenous protein, further validating our knockout/re-expression approach. Most importantly, this system can be used to generate gene-edited primary T cells for in vivo studies, such as the quantification of anti-tumor responses. Our knockout and re-expression platform provides a useful gene editing tool for primary T cells in fundamental research and immunotherapy development.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Prenatal opioid exposure (POE) is an escalating public health concern. However, its impact on neonatal immune development remains poorly defined. This study examined how POE, with or without maternal hepatitis C (hepatitis C virus, HCV) infection, shapes neonatal immunity. METHODS: Umbilical cord blood was collected from pregnancies included uncomplicated term controls (n=38) and deliveries in patients with severe opioid use disorder on medication-assisted treatment, with (n=41) or without HCV (n=34) infection. Flow cytometry was used to characterize cell phenotype and functional response to stimulation. Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to investigate transcriptomics changes. RESULTS: POE was associated with smaller birth size, higher rates of congenital anomalies, and longer intensive care admissions. Immune profiling showed a proinflammatory milieu, reduced circulating levels of neuroprotective factors, expanded memory/effector T and B cells, blunted T-cell responses, and markedly reduced natural killer (NK) cell frequency and cytotoxicity, especially in POE HCV+ newborns. Monocytes exhibited inflammatory reprogramming with impaired antiviral and tissue repair pathways and disrupted lymphoid-innate immune cell communication. DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that POE-driven immune disequilibrium may underlie adverse early-life outcomes and highlight monitoring and intervention targets.

papers.abstract_en: Glioma remains largely refractory to immune-checkpoint blockade, in part because tumor-intrinsic mechanisms sustain programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and reinforce an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Tripartite motif-containing 14 (TRIM14) is an immune associated protein. However, the role of TRIM14 in PD-L1 homeostasis in glioma is incompletely defined. Here we reported that TRIM14 was increased in malignancies and was particularly associated with overall survival in glioma. Single-nucleus analysis showed that TRIM14-positive nuclei were predominantly malignant, indicating association between TRIM14 and glioma progression. We also found TRIM14 upregulated PD-L1 protein levels without materially changing CD274 mRNA in glioma cells. Additionally, knockout of TRIM14 reduced tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, TRIM14 recruits deubiquitinase BRCC3 to reduce K63-linked ubiquitination of PD-L1 in glioma cells, thereby inhibiting p62-mediated autophagic degradation of PD-L1. This pathway prompts that TRIM14 or BRCC3 maybe candidate targets for therapeutic intervention in glioma.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) alter host immunity and may produce pathogen-specific susceptibility to neuroinvasive infection. Comparative evidence is limited because events are rare and postmarketing research focuses mainly on progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). METHODS: We analyzed deduplicated US FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports from 2004Q1 to 2025Q4 using a prespecified case-non-case design. Tier A comprised direct high-certainty non-PML neuroinvasive infection terms. Tier B comprised a possible CNS infectious syndrome plus pathogen evidence elsewhere in the report, without CNS confirmation; tier A+B was a lower-certainty expanded endpoint for sensitivity and pathogen composition analyses. We estimated overall reporting (E1), pathogen composition within tier A+B (E2), and same-pathogen CNS localization (E3). Five DMT mechanisms were compared with contemporaneous active DMTs using calendar-year Mantel-Haenszel reporting odds ratios and covariate-adjusted Jeffreys-prior penalized logistic models. RESULTS: Among 492,514 reports, 675 were tier A and 82 additional reports were tier B. Tier A aRORs (95% CIs) were 0.82 (0.63-1.05) for anti-CD20 therapies, 1.77 (1.44-2.16) for S1P modulators, 1.32 (1.06-1.64) for natalizumab, 3.28 (2.24-4.66) for alemtuzumab, and 0.56 (0.21-1.19) for cladribine. Fingolimod accounted for 145 of 152 S1P cases and had an aROR of 2.15 (1.75-2.64). Among four mechanisms eligible for E2, pathogen composition differed (LRT 210.59, 9 df; bootstrap P = 9.99 × 10-4): viral reports were enriched with anti-CD20 therapies (OR 4.24, 2.56-7.02) and natalizumab (2.03, 1.26-3.26), fungal reports with S1P modulators (29.09, 15.77-53.64), and bacterial reports with alemtuzumab (4.99, 2.27-11.01). Only natalizumab-HSV/VZV met the adjusted E3 gate and showed CNS enrichment (aROR 2.80, 1.80-4.38; Holm-adjusted P = 5.81 × 10-6). CONCLUSIONS: E1 contrasts were interpreted as separate reporting comparisons, not a formal equality test across mechanisms. S1P reporting was largely fingolimod-driven, and natalizumab-HSV/VZV was the only prespecified pair with adjusted same-pathogen CNS enrichment. Findings support targeted vigilance and confirmatory studies but do not estimate incidence or establish causality.

papers.abstract_en: The transition from menstruation to endometrial regeneration is a dynamic biological interval involving inflammatory resolution, immune-cell regulation, epithelial repair, vascular remodeling, and endocrine-dependent tissue renewal. Although these processes are individually well established, it remains unclear whether measurable variation in the peri-menstrual endometrial immune transition predicts subsequent endometrial differentiation, receptivity, or implantation within the same cycle. This unresolved question defines the primary focus of the present framework. This article proposes the Immunological Purity Theory, a testable conceptual framework in which immunological purity refers to the transition from menstrual-associated inflammatory and reparative activity toward a regulated endometrial state compatible with subsequent receptivity. The term does not denote sterility, absence of immune activity, complete absence of inflammation, or an established clinical condition. The core hypothesis proposes that interindividual and intraindividual variation in the timing, coordination, or characteristics of this immune-repair transition may prospectively relate to the subsequent trajectory of endometrial regeneration, hormone-dependent differentiation, receptivity, and implantation. The framework does not assume that menstrual inflammation persists until implantation. Rather, it proposes a testable within-cycle relationship between an early endometrial immune-repair phenotype and the later receptive state of the same tissue. This distinction is important because menstruation occurs during the early follicular phase, whereas implantation occurs during the mid-secretory phase. Accordingly, prospective studies are required to determine whether early-cycle immune-repair characteristics provide reproducible information about later endometrial function beyond normal cycle-dependent variation. Placental adaptation, epigenetic programming, and neurodevelopment are presented as sequential downstream extensions of the core reproductive hypothesis rather than established consequences of peri-menstrual immune variation. Current evidence provides biological plausibility for individual components of these pathways but does not validate the complete proposed sequence, and no direct evidence currently links peri-menstrual endometrial immune variation to autism spectrum disorder. The framework therefore prioritizes characterization of reproducible peri-menstrual immune-repair phenotypes and their prospective relationships with receptivity and implantation before investigation of more distal developmental outcomes. The Immunological Purity Theory is presented as a falsifiable research framework requiring direct empirical validation and should not be interpreted as clinical guidance regarding conception timing or neurodevelopmental risk.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Blood-spinal cord barrier (BSCB) disruption and neuroinflammation contribute to secondary injury after spinal cord injury (SCI). Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and human adipose-derived stem cells (hADSCs) each show therapeutic potential, but the effects of combined treatment and the influence of fecal soluble components on hADSCs secretory activity remain unclear. METHODS: A T9 forceps-crush SCI model was established in C57BL/6J mice to compare FMT, intralesional hADSCs transplantation, and their combination. Functional recovery, BSCB permeability, neuroinflammation, lesion pathology, and neural tissue preservation were evaluated. Exploratory 16S rRNA sequencing was performed at 35 days post-injury. In vitro, hADSCs were exposed to filtered fecal material from healthy donor mice, and their conditioned medium was applied to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-injured bEnd.3 endothelial cells. RESULTS: Combined FMT and hADSCs treatment improved locomotor recovery, attenuated BSCB leakage and neuroinflammatory responses, and preserved neural tissue, with several outcomes greater than either monotherapy. Exploratory 16S analysis identified treatment-associated differences in microbial richness and overall community composition. Fecal-filtrate preconditioning increased hADSCs secretion of VEGF, HGF, and IL-10 by 2.3-, 2.2-, and 1.8-fold, respectively. Conditioned medium from preconditioned hADSCs improved wound closure, preserved ZO-1 and Claudin-5 signals, and reduced endothelial monolayer permeability after OGD/R. IL-10 silencing partially attenuated these protective effects. CONCLUSIONS: Combined FMT and hADSCs treatment was associated with greater BSCB preservation, reduced neuroinflammation, and improved functional recovery after SCI. In vitro, soluble components of healthy-donor fecal filtrate modulated hADSCs secretory activity and enhanced endothelial protection. These findings do not establish that oral FMT reprograms transplanted hADSCs in vivo or that microbiota alterations mediate the combined therapeutic effect.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder frequently accompanied by gut dysbiosis and neurobehavioral comorbidities, but the microbial metabolites mediating gut-skin crosstalk remain unclear. We investigated whether preventive administration of Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis HEM20-01 attenuates the development of AD-like phenotypes and characterized the accompanying gut microbiome, succinate, intestinal, and behavioral alterations. METHODS: HEM20-01 was orally administered to NC/Nga mice beginning 2 weeks before house dust mite (HDM) induction and continued throughout the 4-week induction period. Cutaneous and intestinal inflammation were assessed by histology, gene expression, and multiplex cytokine analysis, and behavior by the open field test. Fecal microbiota composition and metabolite profiles were analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and gas chromatography-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (GC-TOF-MS)-based metabolomics. Exogenous succinate was administered in an independent MC903-induced dermatitis model to test whether succinate can aggravate these responses. RESULTS: HDM-induced AD-like mice showed activation of the intestinal succinate receptor 1 (SUCNR1)-tuft cell-IL-25 axis and enrichment of the putative succinate-associated family Rikenellaceae and its genus Alistipes, together with elevated fecal and plasma succinate. Preventive HEM20-01 administration attenuated the development of cutaneous and intestinal inflammatory phenotypes. HEM20-01-treated mice also showed a lower relative abundance of putative succinate-associated taxa (Bacteroidaceae, Rikenellaceae, Christensenellaceae, Bacteroides, and Alistipes), lower circulating succinate levels, reduced activation of SUCNR1-tuft cell-IL-25-related signaling, and attenuated behavioral and hippocampal serotonergic alterations compared with untreated AD-like mice. In a separate MC903-induced dermatitis model, succinate supplementation exacerbated cutaneous and intestinal inflammation. CONCLUSIONS: Preventive HEM20-01 administration attenuates the development of AD-like phenotypes and associated behavioral alterations, accompanied by changes in gut microbiome composition, lower circulating succinate, and intestinal inflammatory signaling.

papers.abstract_en: Periodontitis is a dysbiotic inflammatory disease characterized by progressive periodontal destruction, in which neutrophils play a central but functionally diverse role. IL-17A is closely linked to neutrophil-mediated host responses; however, how IL-17A deficiency reshapes neutrophil heterogeneity during periodontitis remains unclear. Here, we established a Porphyromonas gingivalis-induced experimental periodontitis model in wild-type and IL-17A knockout mice and integrated micro-CT, histology, 16S rRNA sequencing, and single-cell RNA sequencing to define the consequences of IL-17A loss in the periodontal microenvironment. IL-17A deficiency exacerbated alveolar bone loss and osteoclast accumulation and was associated with altered oral microbial composition consistent with dysbiosis. Single-cell profiling revealed marked remodeling of the immune landscape, with impaired neutrophil accumulation and altered neutrophil subset composition in IL-17A-deficient periodontal tissues. Neutrophils from IL-17A knockout mice showed reduced inflammatory chemokine/cytokine programs and a shift toward antimicrobial granule-associated, extracellular matrix-responsive, and TGF-β/THBS-linked transcriptional states. Trajectory, transcriptional regulatory, and cell-cell communication analyses further demonstrated that IL-17A deficiency disrupted neutrophil state transitions and attenuated neutrophil-centered CCL, CXCL, TNF, SELPG, and ICAM signaling while enhancing matrix-associated communication pathways. Together, these findings identify IL-17A deficiency as a driver of neutrophil reprogramming and aggravated periodontal destruction and indicate an association with microbial dysbiosis, providing single-cell-level insight into the IL-17A-neutrophil axis in dysbiotic periodontitis.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Fulfilling a vision that extends beyond their role as antibiotic alternatives, bacteriophages are now recognized as active immunomodulators, a concept aligning with early hypotheses of their biological activity. In addition to their bactericidal action, these properties require detailed investigation. This study aims to characterize the immunomodulatory effects of bacteriophages on pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine production by human immune cells isolated from healthy blood donors. METHODS: We assessed the secretion of a comprehensive panel of 11 cytokines (including IFN-γ, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10) by peripheral blood mononuclear cells and their isolated subpopulations (B and T lymphocytes, helper and cytotoxic T lymphocytes, natural killer cells, and monocytes). The cells were incubated for 24 hours with purified Escherichia coli phage T4 and therapeutic staphylococcal phage A5/80. Reference cells were incubated with lipopolysaccharide from E. coli B at a concentration corresponding to its activity in the applied phage preparations. For comparison, we also assessed cytokine responses to human adenovirus 5, used as a benchmark for a virus capable of infecting human cells. RESULTS: Cell-specific analysis revealed a distinct hierarchy in immune responsiveness: our data suggest that monocytes may act as the primary sensors driving cytokine signatures, while we did not confirm a discernible direct response in B, natural killer, and cytotoxic T cells. Importantly, the magnitude of these responses was markedly lower than the robust inflammatory cytokine secretion triggered by human adenovirus 5, providing context for the phage-induced effects relative to a viral infection of human cells and underscoring the limited inflammatory footprint of therapeutic phages. CONCLUSION: These results improve our understanding of phage-human immune system interactions, which is important for appreciating their broader impact on human homeostasis and for assessing the safety of phage therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune rejection is a major cause of graft dysfunction following organ transplantation, and CD4+ T cells play a critical role in this process. Esculetin is a natural coumarin compound derived from the Chinese herbal medicine Fraxinus. Although its anti-tumor and anti-inflammatory effects have been extensively investigated, its potential role in transplant immunology remains unexplored. METHODS: The effect of esculetin on transplant rejection and CD4+ T cells was evaluated by survival curve analysis, H&E staining, immunohistochemical staining, flow cytometry, and RNA sequencing. The effects of esculetin on the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-protein kinase B (AKT)-mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, cell cycle, apoptosis, and glycolytic metabolism in CD4+ T cells were also examined. The functional rescue experiments were performed by combining esculetin with the PI3K activator 740Y-P and inhibitor LY294002. RESULTS: Esculetin prolonged graft survival and attenuated graft injury. In addition, esculetin treatment suppressed CD4+ T cell functional responses. RNA sequencing of cultured CD4+ T cells revealed that genes downregulated by esculetin were enriched in the PI3K-AKT and cell cycle pathways. Mechanistically, esculetin inhibited PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling, glycolysis, and cell cycle progression, while promoting apoptosis in CD4+ T cells. Furthermore, rescue experiments using PI3K modulators confirmed that esculetin acts through this pathway to suppress proliferation, induce apoptosis, and prolong graft survival. CONCLUSIONS: The present study is the first to demonstrate that esculetin attenuates immune rejection in mouse skin and heart transplantation models by modulating the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway in CD4+ T cells, thereby exerting inhibitory effects on proliferation, induction of apoptosis, and suppression of glycolytic metabolism.

papers.abstract_en: Initially, we reported that hemolysin BL (HBL) secreted from Bacillus toyonensis BV-17 showed potent antitumor activity in both in vitro and in vivo models, inducing rapid tumor cell lysis and immune activation. However, its non-specific cytotoxicity posed challenges for clinical application. To address this, we engineered HBL by fusing the single-chain variable fragment (scFv) of an anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody to each of the three protein components of HBL, creating an immunotoxin termed EGFR-targeted HBL (EGFR-HBL). This modification enabled EGFR-HBL to specifically kill EGFR-positive tumor cells in a dose-dependent manner, while losing cytotoxicity against EGFR-negative cells. Notably, neither individual fusion proteins (anti-EGFR scFv-HBL-B, anti-EGFR scFv-HBL-L1, and anti-EGFR scFv-HBL-L2) nor any pairwise combinations exhibited cytotoxicity; cytotoxicity was only observed when all three recombinant proteins were co-expressed. In PBMCs co-cultured experiments, EGFR-HBL enhanced CD4+ (41% vs. 34%) and CD8+ (13.6% vs. 9.4%) T cell proportion and elevated TNF-α levels, which was only validated in vitro. In vivo experiments demonstrated that intratumoral injection of EGFR-HBL significantly reduced tumor volume by 66% compared to controls. The intraperitoneal injection treatment group also demonstrated comparable efficacy, with both groups primarily exhibiting necrosis of tumor tissues and extensive inflammatory cell infiltration.

papers.abstract_en: The tumor-stroma percentage (TSP) has been proposed as a prognostic factor in ovarian cancer. When assessed manually by pathologists, the TSP can be subject to significant inter-rater variability. Automated methods for TSP determination have recently been developed. Existing approaches typically yield a single TSP value for a relatively small region of interest in the slide, introducing bias through region selection and potentially overlooking the TSP distribution across the entire histologically examined area. We present an adaptable deep learning pipeline, efficiently fine-tuned for ovarian cancer tissue analysis using a few-shot learning approach, requiring only minimal new training annotations. Instead of calculating a single TSP value, our method quantifies the global TSP distribution across the entire tumor and therefore captures its spatial heterogeneity. To identify a prognostic biomarker, we systematically evaluated a panel of metrics describing this distribution in 98 patients. Our analysis revealed that the mean-median difference of the TSP distribution [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.60, 95% CI = 0.46-0.79, p < 0.001], a quantitative measure of asymmetry, together with the mean TSP (HR = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.43-0.97, p = 0.03), are biomarkers significantly associated with recurrence-free survival. By successfully adapting a pipeline for ovarian cancer, we demonstrate that automated analysis of the entire TSP distribution provides significant prognostic information superior to that obtained by manual assessment. Spatial heterogeneity of the TSP is a key prognostic factor. © 2026 Fraunhofer IIS and The Author(s). papers.abstract_en: The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is a conserved and compelling target for pan-coronavirus antiviral development. To date, all US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved RdRp inhibitors are nucleotide inhibitors (NIs), which are prone to drug resistance and show limited clinical efficacy. Developing alternative non-nucleotide inhibitors (NNIs) with high target specificity, structural diversity, and metabolic stability could yield more effective antivirals. Here, we identify an allosteric RdRp NNI, BAY-850, via computational screening. BAY-850 exhibits potent, broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants and other human coronaviruses. Mechanistic studies show that BAY-850 binds directly to a previously unrecognized allosteric site on nsp12, thereby fine-tuning the catalytic motif F loop out-conformation the orthosteric site. Importantly, therapeutic administration of BAY-850 significantly reduces viral loads in the nasal turbinates and lungs of SARS-CoV-2-infected K18-hACE2 mice. These findings validate a novel allosteric site in RdRp and support BAY-850 as a start-point for broad-spectrum anti-coronavirus development.

papers.abstract_en: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a complex autoimmune disease and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), given their unique immune-modulatory potential, have emerged as a promising route for treating LN. Understanding the multiscale dynamic LN-MSC interactions and selecting the optimal clinical design for MSCs is critical to enhance their therapeutic potential and achieve meaningful benefit-risk differentiation in patients. To guide MSC clinical development, we constructed the first mechanistic quantitative systems pharmacology model of LN pathophysiology that integrated multimodal preclinical-clinical data, with detailed illustration of standard-of-care immunosuppressant pharmacology and physiologically-based biodistribution and therapeutic mechanisms of MSCs. We created model-based virtual LN patients that well captured clinical interpatient heterogeneity and were validated by numerous sets of clinical efficacy readouts, including first-hand results from our investigator-initiated trial testing MSCs in LN patients. We used this computational framework and identified that a spaced two-infusion MSC dosing strategy would yield optimal clinical response in LN patients, which directly informed the phase 2 design of a novel MSC therapy. Modeling analyses further identified that CXCL10 in combination with proteinuria are potential predictive biomarkers that could boost clinical renal response to MSCs. These results demonstrated the exceptional importance of our QSP framework in driving MSC clinical development for LN patients.

papers.abstract_en: Immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment landscape for many cancers, but fails to improve the outcomes of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), in which low tumor antigen presentation restricts the recognition and eradication of cancerous cells by immunocytes. We here report an approach to in situ reprogramming hypoimmunogenic glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) into type 1 conventional dendritic cell (cDC1)-like cells for presenting endogenous tumor antigens and priming sustained tumoricidal T-cell responses. Specifically, our cavity-injectable nucleobase-derived lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-hydrogel superstructure efficiently delivers transcription factors (PU.1, IRF8, BATF3) and the costimulatory molecule (TNFSF9) into GSCs to induce cDC1-like reprogramming. These cDC1-like cells potentiate GBM immunogenicity, elicit robust adaptive immunity and long-term antitumor memory, thereby inhibiting tumor growth and preventing postoperative GBM relapse in mice. Collectively, this work establishes in situ tumor cell reprogramming into licensed cDC1-like cells as a therapeutic paradigm for converting immunologically "cold" tumors into a self-vaccinating immune niche with broad translational potential for hypoimmunogenic malignancy treatment.

papers.abstract_en: Barrington's nucleus (Bar) is a brainstem hub essential for lower urinary tract (LUT) function, yet the molecular identity and functional specialization of its neuronal subtypes remain poorly defined. Here, we construct a single-nucleus transcriptional atlas of the murine Bar and identify an excitatory Penk-expressing population (Bar-Penk) critical for LUT regulation. Bar-Penk neurons are selectively active during voiding, when the external urethral sphincter (EUS) relaxes, and their optogenetic activation elicits time-locked suppression of EUS activity. Chemogenetic activation of these neurons induces a sex-specific, aberrant pattern of micturition, whereas targeted ablation impairs voluntary marking behavior in response to female cues. We observe multiple regions involved in visceromotor regulation and behavioral state control that project to Bar-Penk neurons, supporting their role as integrators of internal state and environmental context that drive urinary output. These findings provide new insights into the brainstem circuits that shape reflexive and voluntary micturition and highlight how discrete neuronal subtypes contribute to sexually dimorphic regulation of LUT function.

papers.abstract_en: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a lethal pediatric brain tumor with limited therapeutic options and a poor prognosis. The success of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy requires both improving T cell tumor infiltration and persistence and reducing the risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Here, we adapted and advanced a brain-restricted CAR T cell platform previously validated in glioblastoma to address the anatomical and biological challenges of DMG. We engineered a T cell circuit in which a brain-specific synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptor recognizing brevican (BCAN) induced CAR expression against EphA2 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC"), thereby restricting CAR expression to the central nervous system (CNS). In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival. An alternative BCAN-primed CAR targeting B7-H3 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC-B/I") similarly improved therapeutic efficacy when delivered intravenously. However, icv administration triggered fatal neurotoxicity because of low-level B7-H3 expression in nontumor CNS regions, indicating that rapid CNS exposure via icv delivery can amplify off-tumor toxicity. In contrast, in an immunocompetent syngeneic DMG model, both iv and icv delivery of a murinized BCAN-gated B7-H3 CAR (mB-SYNC-B7-H3) achieved durable tumor clearance and resistance to rechallenge without any detectable neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, synNotch-primed CAR T cells exhibited reduced exhaustion, enhanced activation, and enrichment of naïve and stem cell memory-like subsets. These findings demonstrate that brain-sensing synNotch CAR T circuits represent a generalizable and translatable strategy for targeting multiple CNS malignancies, including DMG.

papers.abstract_en: The cohesin complex is well recognized for maintaining sister chromatid cohesion during mitosis and meiosis, as well as for its role in genome organization through chromatin loop formation. Recent studies indicate that cohesin can be co-opted in cancer by aiding DNA repair processes to promote cancer cell proliferation. However, the mechanisms, protein partners, and functions by which cohesin is involved in DNA repair remain unclear. Here, we uncover a novel function of cohesin core subunits (RAD21, STAG1/2) in promoting transcription-coupled homologous recombination (TC-HR) at sites of R-loops. We demonstrate that cohesin (SMC1/3, RAD21, STAG1) preferentially localizes to R-loops in vitro and localize to DNA damage-induced R-loops in cells. Through a screen of chromatin remodelers, we identify that chromatin remodeler SMARCA5 recruits RAD21 and STAG at R-loop sites. SMARCA5 forms a complex with RAD21 via its SLIDE domain and is recruited to R-loops, providing a dual mechanism to promote the R-loop localization of the cohesin core subunits. The ATPase activity of SMARCA5 facilitates the localization of RAD21 and RAD51 at sites of R-loops to promote TC-HR and timely resolution of R-loops. Depletion of either core subunits of cohesin or SMARCA5, both of which are overexpressed in a subset of cancers, leads to aberrant R-loop accumulation, stalled replication fork progression, and elevated transcription-replication collision (TRC) events induced cell death. These findings shed new light on a previously unknown function of SMARCA5 through regulating cohesin core subunits RAD21/STAG at R-loops and established their potential as therapeutic targets in treating cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer with a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This study investigated the role of matrix Gla protein (MGP)-high cancer-associated fibroblasts (MGPhi CAFs) in melanoma progression and their potential relevance to immunotherapy. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing and tissue validation were used to characterize MGP expression, and its association with prognosis was analyzed. In vitro assays and mouse melanoma models were used to investigate the effects of MGPhi CAFs on tumor progression, myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) recruitment and apoptosis. The role of MDSCs was further examined by adoptive transfer. The antitumor effects of vitamin K2, anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) and their combination were evaluated in vivo. Normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Group differences were analyzed using two-tailed paired or unpaired Student’s t-tests or one-way or two-way analysis of variance followed by Tukey’s multiple comparisons test. Survival curves were compared using the log-rank test. RESULTS: MGP expression was reduced in melanoma tissues, and low MGP expression was associated with poor prognosis. MGPhi CAFs inhibited melanoma cell proliferation and migration and suppressed tumor growth. Mechanistically, MGPhi CAFs reduced C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2/C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2-mediated MDSC recruitment and promoted MDSC apoptosis by inhibiting tumor necrosis factor receptor 2-cellular FLICE-like inhibitory protein signaling and activating caspase-8. Adoptive transfer of MDSCs reversed the antitumor effects of MGPhi CAFs. Vitamin K2 increased MGP protein levels in CAFs isolated from tumors. Combined vitamin K2 and anti-PD-1 treatment produced greater antitumor activity than either monotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: MGPhi CAFs suppress melanoma progression by reducing MDSC recruitment and survival. These findings identify an MGPhi CAF-MDSC regulatory axis and support further evaluation of vitamin K2 combined with anti-PD-1 therapy in melanoma.

papers.abstract_en: Nucleoside analogues are among the most promising broad-spectrum antiviral agents. We developed a high-throughput synergistic screening system to identify US Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs that enhance the effectiveness of nucleoside analogues. Unlike conventional combination approaches, this strategy does not require boost agents to have direct antiviral activity; instead, they can enhance antiviral agent's effect through novel synergistic mechanisms. We identified mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), which significantly boosts ribavirin's (RBV) antiviral efficacy against influenza A virus, even at concentrations where MMF alone shows minimal activity. MMF enhances RBV by inhibiting IMPDH (inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase) and reducing cellular GTP levels, potentially increasing RBV incorporation and its antiviral potency. This mechanism was confirmed by adding exogenous GTP, which reversed the synergy. In a mouse model, MMF also enhanced RBV's effectiveness against PR8 in vivo. Moreover, MMF showed synergistic effects against other influenza subtypes and RNA viruses including ZIKV and HCoV-OC43, demonstrating the potential wide applicability of this strategy. Our study introduces a new screening system and identifies novel RBV combinations, offering a promising approach for developing effective broad-spectrum antiviral combinations against emerging viral threats.

papers.abstract_en: Antibody‒cell conjugates (ACCs) represent a promising therapeutic strategy emerging in the biopharmaceutical industry to overcome the limitations of current immunotherapies. ACCs constitute a novel class of living drugs developed by anchoring functional antibodies onto the surface of living cells via specific linkers or conjugation methods. These carrier cells encompass both immune effector cells (such as Natural Killer cells, γδ T cells, and activated T cells) and non-immune cells (such as erythrocytes and platelets). Distinct from genetic engineering, ACCs directly modify the cell surface using chemical biology, enzymatic catalysis, or physical assembly, thereby endowing cells with precise tumor-targeting capabilities while preserving their intrinsic biological functions. This technology facilitates the scalable production of "off-the-shelf" therapeutics and has shown promising potential in treating both hematological malignancies and refractory solid tumors with a superior safety profile. This review systematically examines the current construction strategies and carrier cell selection for ACCs, covering both immune effector cells and non-immune carrier cells, and discusses the clinical progress, key challenges, and future directions.

papers.abstract_en: Single-cell chromatin accessibility offers unique insights into transcriptional regulation beyond gene expression. However, paired datasets of these two modalities remain relatively scarce, and existing computational models cannot simultaneously predict chromatin accessibility for unseen genomic regions and cells. Here, we present XChrom, a deep learning framework for genome-wide cross-cell chromatin accessibility prediction that integrates genomic sequence and single-cell transcriptomics-derived cell identity into a unified model. Comprehensive evaluations show that XChrom consistently outperforms existing methods in cross-region and cross-cell predictions, and uniquely enables cross-both predictions. It also supports cross-sample prediction when batch effects are properly corrected. Cross-species analyses demonstrate XChrom's robust performance and its ability to capture evolutionarily conserved regulatory rules. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells from COVID-19 patients, XChrom accurately identifies transcription factor activities in novel but related cell states and reveals pathogenesis-associated regulatory alterations. XChrom is available as an open-source Python package, facilitating single-cell transcriptional regulation research.

papers.abstract_en: Chemotherapy remains the mainstay treatment of many solid cancers; however, resistance and recurrence compromise patient outcomes. We investigated chemotherapy resistance mechanisms in Triple Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) by examining cells that survive chemotherapy-induced apoptotic caspase activation. Using a biosensor that permanently labels cells surviving executioner caspase activation with GFP, we identified a GFP+ population that survives transient paclitaxel treatment. These GFP+ cells display a stem-like invasive phenotype, altered mitochondrial metabolism, and increased drug resistance. Metabolomics profiling identified defects in TCA cycle metabolites and accumulation of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs). Mechanistically, surviving GFP+ cells exhibited Epithelial to Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) and ZEB1-regulated repression of GPX4 expression, resulting in increased sensitivity to ferroptotic cell death. Consistent with this, transforming growth factor- beta induced EMT also suppressed GPX4 and increased ferroptosis sensitivity in Normal Mouse Mammary epithelial cells. ZEB1 knockdown strongly reduced the GFP+ surviving fraction, identifying ZEB1 as a key regulator of apoptotic survival. Supplementation with arachidonic acid restored survival in ZEB1 knockdown cells, while the ferroptosis-protective drug, Ferrostatin-1, prevented the accumulation of GFP+ survivors, demonstrating that ferroptosis sensitivity is required for the survival of TNBC cells from chemotherapy-induced apoptosis. Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized link between ferroptosis and apoptosis and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic vulnerabilities in a subset of chemotherapy-resistant TNBC.

papers.abstract_en: Tumor progression arises from tightly coupled cellular, vascular, metabolic, immune, and biomechanical processes within the tumor microenvironment (TME), forming a heterogeneous multiscale system that cannot be fully characterized through experimental observation alone. Computational modeling provides a quantitative framework for integrating these mechanisms, but the diversity of available methods complicates model selection, parameterization, validation, and clinical translation. This review presents a problem-driven synthesis of computational approaches for TME modeling. Continuous, discrete, and discrete-continuous hybrid paradigms are compared in terms of biological resolution, data requirements, interpretability, and computational cost, and are linked to five mechanistic domains: tumor-cell dynamics, vascular transport, extracellular matrix and mechanics, metabolism and hypoxia, and immune interactions. Model credibility is examined through parameter identifiability, uncertainty quantification, numerical validity, biological fidelity, and clinical relevance, with emphasis on interpreting performance according to intended use and validation context. Machine learning is analyzed by function within mechanistic-ML integration: surrogate models accelerate forward simulation, inverse methods estimate latent parameters and states, patient-specific workflows combine multimodal clinical data with mechanistic models, and physics-informed neural networks embed governing equations into learning. We further discuss longitudinal personalization, physics-aware multiscale integration, clinically deployable digital twins, external generalization, and synthetic-data-to-clinical transfer. A translation-readiness pathway is proposed from mechanistic hypothesis generation to adaptive digital-twin decision support. Credible TME modeling should prioritize the minimum sufficient model, explicit intended use, transparent uncertainty, and evidence matched to the biological or clinical question.

papers.abstract_en: Tungsten-dependent formate dehydrogenases are among the most active biological catalysts for carbon dioxide reduction, but their production is limited by complex metal cofactor requirements and poor compatibility with standard expression hosts. Here, we address this limitation by engineering an Escherichia coli chassis through reconstruction of tungsten cofactor biosynthesis, installation of a high-affinity tungstate transporter, and reinforcement of iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis. The resulting chassis produces the formate dehydrogenase from Methylorubrum extorquens with native-level specific activity, near-stoichiometric tungsten incorporation, and high volumetric activity, while substantially enhancing whole-cell CO-driven CO₂-to-formate conversion compared with the native-host system. The engineered host demonstrates broad applicability by supporting maturation of tungsten-dependent formate dehydrogenases from Cupriavidus necator, Lutibaculum baratangense, Thermococcus onnurineus, and Thermoanaerobacter kivui. In this work, we show that engineering host metal cofactor metabolism provides a strategy for aerobic production of active tungsten-dependent formate dehydrogenases, expanding access to this enzyme family for biological and biotechnological applications.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cancer immunotherapy, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, and bispecific antibodies, has transformed the treatment of advanced malignancies, yet primary and acquired resistance remain major barriers to durable benefit. Across these therapies, resistance reflects the failure of one or more of three shared requirements for effective antitumor immunity: tumor immune visibility, lost through defective antigen presentation and interferon signaling; immune access to tumor nests, restricted by stromal and vascular barriers; and effector cell function, undermined by suppressive myeloid and regulatory populations, metabolic restriction, and loss of tertiary lymphoid structures. MAIN BODY: In this review, we argue that resistance to targeted therapies, endocrine therapies, and PARP inhibitors should not be treated as a problem separate from immunotherapy resistance. Rather, these resistant states often converge on the same three axes that govern immunotherapy resistance (immune visibility, access, and effector function), yielding a unified framework across therapeutic classes. Using canonical immunotherapy resistance as a reference model, we examine how osimertinib resistance, androgen receptor (AR)-pathway-resistant states, and BRCA reversion-mediated PARP inhibitor resistance may remodel these same immune-evasion axes. Targeted therapy resistance provides the most complete case, with epithelial-mesenchymal transition, PD-L1 upregulation, STING suppression, and immune exclusion extending across all three axes. AR pathway reactivation shows plausible links to immune remodeling through direct MHC-I repression and myeloid reprogramming, although the clinical evidence base remains less mature. BRCA reversion illustrates a mechanistically suggestive dual-valence state in which restored DNA repair may diminish innate immune sensing while also generating computationally predicted junctional neopeptides whose immunogenicity remains to be validated. CONCLUSIONS: By reframing resistance as a new immune state that converges on the same three immune-evasion axes rather than a terminal event, this review shifts attention from why a therapy failed to which immune-evasion axis now predominates and how it might be countered. This perspective supports mechanism-matched combination therapy, adaptive molecular monitoring, and cautious exploitation of vulnerabilities generated by the resistant state itself. As an organizing model rather than a claim of uniform causality, the framework now requires prospective validation.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate, multiplexed microRNA detection is critical for early cancer diagnosis. We present a droplet-based digital CRISPR/Cas13a platform for simultaneous, amplification-free detection of multiple miRNAs. By integrating double emulsion (DE) microfluidics with programmable crRNAs, the system achieves orthogonal, interference-free readouts, enabling precise absolute quantification in complex biological samples. The assay demonstrates high sequence specificity, robust orthogonality, and consistent performance across target combinations and matrices. Fluorescence-positive droplet counts correlate linearly with input concentrations, allowing quantification of miRNA-21, miRNA-29a, and miRNA-92a with 10 copies/μL representing the lowest concentration experimentally evaluated in this study. The applicability of the platform is further evaluated in a small proof-of-concept cohort of plasma samples from healthy controls and colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. This platform provides an amplification-free approach for multiplexed miRNA quantification and supports further development for clinical biomarker analysis.

papers.authors: Betts BC, Savid-Frontera C, McSain S, Walton K, Maybee E, Beatty N, Goala P, Massillon D et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Medicine, Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center, Buffalo, New York, USA brian.betts@roswellpark.org marco.davila@rosw…
papers.authors_conclusion: 临床前证据支持进一步转化研究CD83 CAR T用于B细胞白血病和淋巴瘤；其优势包括B细胞再生障碍风险低，以及CD19 CAR T暴露后仍有效。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR T) targeting CD19 can cure patients with aggressive B cell malignancies. Relapse due to CD19 loss and infections from B cell aplasia remain major causes of death after CD19 CAR T. We demonstrate that CD83 is a clinically relevant target for CAR T therapy in B cell malignancies, overcoming limitations of CD19 CAR T. METHODS: We evaluate CD83 expression among B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL), and circulating healthy B cells, compared with CD19, CD20, and CD22. We test the activity of CD19 and CD83 CAR T against Raji and Nalm6 target cells using in vitro and in vivo preclinical models. Functional and immunophenotypic aspects of CD19 and CD83 CAR T are investigated to compare potency. Further, we evaluate CD19 and CD83 expression on B cell ALL after prior CD19-directed therapy, revealing a propensity for CD19 antigen loss. To simulate CD19 antigen loss, we test CD19 and CD83 CAR T against CD19 knock-out Nalm6 cells. RESULTS: CD83 is expressed on B-cell ALL, MCL, and DLBCL, with negligible expression on circulating B cells and CLL. B cell ALL expresses CD83 at diagnosis and on relapse following CD19-directed therapy, when CD19 is decreased. CD83 CAR T kills B cell leukemia/lymphoma cell lines in vitro, providing efficacy after CD19 antigen loss. We show CD83 CAR T is effective as monotherapy in mice. Exploratory experiments suggest CD83 CAR T may offer enhanced efficacy when administered sequentially after CD19 CAR T. CONCLUSIONS: Our preclinical evidence justifies further translational investigation of CD83 CAR T in B cell leukemia and lymphoma. The benefits of CD83 CAR T include a low risk for B cell aplasia and efficacy after exposure to CD19 CAR T.

papers.abstract_en: This study identifies Engineered Water Nanostructures (EWNSs)-electrically charged water nanoparticles containing reactive oxygen species-as a potent non-pharmacological tool for neutralizing Japanese cedar pollen allergens. By exposing pollen and its primary allergen, Cry j 1, to EWNSs, researchers observed a significant reduction in allergenicity within 24 h, effectively preventing dendritic cell activation and suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and TNF-α. In vivo tests on BALB/c mice demonstrated that EWNS treatment significantly lowered IgE levels, inhibited the expansion of Type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2), and attenuated eosinophilic airway inflammation. Furthermore, seven days of EWNS inhalation was associated with higher peripheral oxygen saturation and lower Th2 cytokine expression, without adverse effects in the measured endpoints. These findings support the potential of EWNS pretreatment to lower the immunoreactivity of cedar pollen preparations and indicate short-term anti-inflammatory associations with EWNS inhalation under the conditions tested. Airborne pollen inactivation and comprehensive inhalation safety remain to be established.

papers.abstract_en: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 has led to a global pandemic, causing unprecedented disruption to health systems and economies worldwide, calling for an urgent imperative for precise and sensitive diagnostic method. To address this, a novel detection method, termed antibody‒nucleic acid conjugate linked immunosorbent assay (ANCLISA), was designed for the ultra-sensitive detection of the receptor binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2, which play a pivotal role in the diagnosis of COVID-19. Leveraging the Alphafold 2 model for simulating antibody‒antigen complexes and the ΔΔG predictor model for forecasting the binding free energy of antigen‒antibody complex, we successfully identified the high-affinity antibody TB1. Through the utilization of succinimidyl 4-[N-maleimidomethyl] cyclohexane-1-carboxylate (SMCC) for antibody‒nucleic acid conjugation and the integration of the hybridization chain reaction (HCR) for signal amplification within the system, we have established an ultra-sensitive approach for the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant detection. The proposed immunoassay provided exhibited a linear detection range spanning 11 fg/mL to 11 ng/mL, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.48 fg/mL. Our innovative approach represents a significant stride in enabling precise and ultra-sensitive detection of SARS-CoV-2, thereby holding promise for enhancing diagnostic capabilities in the ongoing global battle against the pandemic.

papers.abstract_en: CARD8 (caspase activation and recruitment domain-containing 8) senses intracellular danger signals, leading to inflammasome formation and pyroptosis. Recently studies have shown that CARD8 was highly expressed in hematopoietic cells, however, the mechanism by which the released C- terminal domain of CARD8 (CARD8-CT) oligomerizes and nucleates, and its role in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treatment has not been fully understood. Here, we identified a long noncoding RNA IL10RB-AS1 as a novel regulator that can enhance the CARD8-CT oligomer assembly and promote pro-caspase-1-dependent pyroptosis in AML cells. Mechanically, IL10RB-AS1 recruits DEAD-box helicase 3, X-linked (DDX3X) to CARD8 and enhances the DDX3X-CARD8 interaction to promote CARD8-CT nucleation. This process activates the CARD8 inflammasome and triggers an ASC-independent pyroptosis response to perturbations in cellular homeostasis. We found that the C-terminal domain of DDX3X is essential for its interaction with both IL10RB-AS1 and CARD8-CT, facilitating inflammasome activation during AML cell pyroptosis. Importantly, IL10RB-AS1 is highly expressed across AML and correlates with poor outcomes. This elevated expression of IL10RB-AS1 promotes DPP8/9 inhibitor induced pro-caspase-1-dependent pyroptosis in vivo, suggesting that high IL10RB-AS1 levels may predict cellular sensitivity to these inhibitors. Our findings not only reveal a novel mechanism by which a lncRNA orchestrates CARD8-CT nucleation but also highlight new therapeutic opportunities for DPP8/9 inhibitors in hematopoietic malignancies with high IL10RB-AS1 expression.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: States have begun implementing waivers that prohibit the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits from being used to purchase selected foods and beverages. We assessed whether these restrictions were associated with changes in the availability of SNAP-authorized convenience stores, supermarkets, and superstores. METHODS: We analyzed repeated observations from 83 697 Census tracts from January 2025 through June 2026. Difference-in-differences models compared changes in retailer availability in states implementing waivers with concurrent changes in states without implemented waivers. RESULTS: Waiver implementation was associated with a 1.4% decline in SNAP-authorized convenience stores, equivalent to 3.0 fewer stores per 100 tracts (95% CI, -5.7 to -0.4; P = 0.03), but not with a significant change in supermarkets or superstores. The largest declines in convenience stores occurred among states restricting beverages and candy (-2.2%; -4.9 stores per 100 tracts; 95% CI, -6.9 to -2.9; P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: The SNAP food restrictions were associated with reduced availability of SNAP-authorized convenience stores but not supermarkets or superstores. Continued monitoring is warranted as these policies expand.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Human adenovirus type 7(HAdV-7) is a major cause of severe pediatric pneumonia, but the mechanisms linking viral infection to pulmonary immune remodeling and lung pathology remain incompletely understood. Progress has been limited by the lack of physiologically relevant animal models that recapitulate human susceptibility. METHODS: We generated human CD46 (hCD46) humanized mice and evaluated pulmonary viral burden, recoverable infectious virus, and lung pathology after HAdV-7 infection. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on lung tissues from wild type and hCD46 humanized mice under control and infected conditions to characterize cellular composition, transcriptional states, and intercellular communication. Human PBMC bulk transcriptomes from pediatric HAdV infection were further analyzed to assess the systemic relevance of mouse lung derived immune programs. RESULTS: hCD46 humanized mice showed increased pulmonary viral burden, recoverable infectious virions, and more severe lung pathology after HAdV-7 infection. Single-cell profiling revealed depletion of resident alveolar macrophages, pronounced expansion of inflammatory macrophage subsets, and remodeling of lymphoid transcriptional states in infected hCD46 lungs. These changes were accompanied by prominent type I/II interferon and interferon associated chemokine programs. B cells and CD4+ and CD8+ T cells showed prominent interferon stimulated genes (ISGs) associated transcriptional states, together with alterations in selected effector- and memory-associated programs and computationally inferred trajectories. Projection of mouse lung derived signatures onto transcriptomes of human peripheral blood mononuclear cell showed that selected interferon associated myeloid and lymphoid programs were also detectable systemically in pediatric HAdV infection. CONCLUSIONS: HAdV-7 infection in hCD46 humanized mice was associated with an interferon enriched pulmonary inflammatory environment, prominent inflammatory myeloid remodeling, and altered lymphoid transcriptional states. This susceptible mouse model provides a useful experimental tool for studying HAdV-7 associated lung disease and for preclinical evaluation of antiviral, immunomodulatory, and vaccine strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) support bone formation through osteogenic differentiation and pro-angiogenic paracrine activity, but the mechanisms coordinating these functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified dual-specificity phosphatase 26 (DUSP26) as a regulator of BMSC osteogenesis and mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 expression increased during osteogenic differentiation and was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissues. p300 gain- and loss-of-function experiments, together with analysis of the Yin Yang1(YY1) K183R mutant, supported the conclusion that p300-regulated YY1 lactylation contributes to DUSP26 transcriptional activation. DUSP26 interacted with the mitochondrial processing peptidase subunit beta(PMPCB) and reduced its tyrosine phosphorylation, with mass spectrometry and mutational analyses implicating Y141 as involved in this regulation. Functional assays supported a model in which DUSP26 limits mitochondrial processing peptidase (MPP)-mediated PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) processing and promotes PINK1-dependent mitophagy, thereby supporting mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 enhanced osteogenic differentiation and the pro-angiogenic activity of BMSC-conditioned medium(CM), whereas its knockdown impaired bone formation and reduced type H vessels in vivo. Furthermore, BMSC-derived exosomes carrying a runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) promoter-driven DUSP26 plasmid produced preferential transgene expression in osteogenic-lineage cells and attenuated ovariectomy-induced bone loss in mice. These findings link lactylation-associated transcriptional regulation to mitochondrial protein processing and support further preclinical evaluation of DUSP26-directed approaches for osteoporosis.

papers.abstract_en: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of long-term neurological disability, and repeated mild TBI (rmTBI) is increasingly linked to chronic neurodegeneration. Clinical evidence suggests that rmTBI creates a prolonged window of vulnerability to further injury. However, the astrocyte-intrinsic mechanisms that convert repeated mechanical stress into delayed neuronal injury remain poorly defined. In particular, whether rmTBI induces a distinct lipid-mediated neurotoxic programme in human astrocytes is unknown. Using a human astrocyte in vitro platform of rmTBI, we deliver controlled repeated mild injuries to astrocytes. Repeated injury induces a distinctive astrocytic phenotype characterised by cytoskeletal remodelling, reactive oxygen species accumulation, biphasic volume changes, extracellular matrix remodelling and lipid droplet formation. Shotgun lipidomics of astrocyte-conditioned medium reveals selective enrichment of bioactive diacylglycerols (DG) following rmTBI. When applied to human cortical neurons, this conditioned medium impairs neuronal function and morphology, increases apoptosis and activates protein kinase C delta (PKCδ). Pharmacological inhibition of PKC attenuates the neurotoxic effect of rmTBI astrocyte-conditioned medium. These findings support a model in which human astrocytes retain a form of 'injury memory' through sustained phenotypic and lipid metabolic remodelling. By implicating the DG-PKCδ axis in delayed neurotoxicity, the study identifies PKC signalling as a tractable target for limiting the long-term consequences of rmTBI. Repeated mild traumatic brain injury induces astrocytic dysfunction, metabolic imbalance and disrupts lipid homeostasis. This leads to the aberrant release of specific diacylglycerol species which activate protein kinase C signalling in neurons and drive delayed neurotoxic cascades.

papers.results: 387例捐献者中362例（93.5%）存在CTE神经病理；选择比中位数4.97（95%CI 4.72-5.26）；偏倚校正后人群死亡时CTE患病率74.5%（95%CI 69.6%-78.3%），保守下限分析为63.7%（57.2%-68.9%）；偏倚校正后生前全因痴呆史患病率27.2%（95%CI 22.6%-31.6%）
papers.authors_conclusion: 本横断面研究结果提示，选择偏倚确实会实质性高估基于捐献者样本的患病率估计，但不太可能完全解释该人群中CTE神经病理的高负担；该病的临床影响仍需进一步研究。
papers.ai_note: 校正值高度依赖选择比估计的正确性，而摘要未说明Poisson模型纳入的协变量、是否处理打球年限/死亡年龄等混杂，也未验证“症状相关捐献”假设；93.5%的捐献者观测值与74.5%的校正值差距主要由模型外推产生，属强假设下的定量偏倚分析而非直接测量。摘要未交代痴呆判定的来源与完整性（死亡索引/家属报告？）、CTE病理评估是否盲法，以及“保守下限”的具体保守化方式。捐献者中387例与捐献者总数396例不一致亦未在摘要中解释。

pico.p: 2008年1月至2023年12月间死亡的已故前NFL球员共2362例（脑捐献者396例、非捐献者1966例；平均打球年限5.1[SD 3.9]年；死亡时≥80岁者971例[41.1%]）；CTE病理分析基于387例捐献者
pico.ic: 暴露：至少参加1场NFL常规赛或季后赛；对照/校正来源：非脑捐献者（用于估计症状相关脑捐献选择比），并以估计的选择比调整捐献者中观察到的CTE神经病理与生前全因痴呆患病率

papers.reason: 与胸外科/胸部肿瘤临床无直接关系，作为方法学范例入册：其“以非捐献者人群估计选择比、再回校外推患病率”的定量偏倚校正框架，可迁移用于胸外科脑库/单中心手术队列（如尸检、切除标本随访队列）中患病率与预后估计的选择偏倚校正，并提示高捐献率来源的单项队列数据不可直接当作人群基线。
papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: The majority of knowledge regarding chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in National Football League (NFL) players is derived from autopsy-based studies on voluntarily donated brains. Because these cohorts are highly vulnerable to selection bias (specifically registry bias), population-level prevalence of CTE among former NFL players is unknown, limiting understanding of the impact of this disease. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the selection-bias adjusted prevalence of CTE neuropathology in deceased NFL players. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This population-based cross-sectional study used Understanding Neurologic Injury and Traumatic Encephalopathy (UNITE) brain bank data combined with National Death Index records on former NFL players. Both brain donor and nondonor NFL players who died between January 2008 and December 2023 were included. Data were analyzed from November 2025 to April 2026. EXPOSURE: Playing in at least 1 regular or postseason NFL game. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes of this study were bias-adjusted prevalence of CTE neuropathology and all-cause dementia among the target population, both of which were measured in donors prior to this study. A cognitive symptom-related brain donation selection ratio (probability of donation given CTE divided by the probability of donation given no CTE) was estimated using Poisson regression and was applied to adjust donor-observed prevalence of CTE neuropathology at death and all-cause dementia during life. The prevalence estimates were adjusted for bias using the estimated selection ratio. RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 2362 deceased former NFL players (mean [SD] years played, 5.1 [3.9]; 971 [41.1%] aged ≥80 years at death), of whom 396 were brain donors and 1966 were nondonors. Of 387 donors, 362 (93.5%) had CTE. The median selection ratio was 4.97 (95% CI, 4.72-5.26). Bias-adjusted population prevalence of CTE at death was 74.5% (95% CI, 69.6%-78.3%), with a conservative lower-bound analysis estimating 63.7% (57.2%-68.9%). Bias-adjusted population prevalence of all-cause dementia history during life was 27.2% (95% CI, 22.6%-31.6%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The findings of this cross-sectional study suggest that selection bias materially inflates donor-based prevalence estimates but is unlikely to fully explain the high burden of CTE neuropathology among this population. Further research is required to understand the clinical impact of this disease.

papers.abstract_en: Ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation is a key environmental risk factor for remodeling the melanoma microenvironment, yet the bidirectional communication mechanisms between keratinocytes and melanoma cells remain incompletely understood. This study developed an in situ monitoring platform integrated with scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM) and a microfluidic chip. With a fabricated Ca2+ ion-selective electrode as a SECM tip (Ca2+-ISE SECM tip), together with a lactate oxidase-modified Pt microelectrode tip (LOx-μPt tip) and a multi-potential step waveform (MPSW) method, the dynamic monitoring of Ca2+, lactate, and ROS in keratinocyte-melanoma cell communication has been achieved. UVB radiation dose-dependently enhanced A-375 melanoma cell migration in both monoculture and co-culture systems. Mechanistically, UVB induced ROS production and stimulated glycolysis in A-375 cells, resulting in elevated lactate release and autocrine-driven migration enhancement. Notably, in the co-culture system, this pro-migratory effect was significantly amplified, while inhibition by the glycolysis inhibitor 2-deoxy-d-glucose (2-DG) was minimal, suggesting a dominant paracrine signaling mechanism. In situ SECM monitoring further demonstrated that UVB also induced ROS generation, transient Ca2+ release, and significantly increased TGF-β1 secretion in HaCaT keratinocytes. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treatment blocked Ca2+ release and TGF-β1 secretion in HaCaT cells, thereby inhibiting co-cultured A-375 cell migration. Further studies confirmed that HaCaT-derived TGF-β1 serves as a key paracrine factor, promoting migration by upregulating YB-1 expression in A-375 cells, a process dependent on extracellular Ca2+. Consequently, this work reveals an intercellular signaling axis in the UVB-exposed skin tumor microenvironment: UVB → ROS → Ca2+ release → TGF-β1 secretion → YB-1 activation, providing new mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for microenvironment-dependent melanoma progression.

papers.abstract_en: Bats tolerate viruses that cause severe disease in humans. Egyptian rousette bats, the natural reservoirs of Marburg virus (MARV), sustain asymptomatic infection, whereas humans develop severe and fatal disease. To define the basis of this divergence, we establish a comparative framework using primary and immortalized Egyptian rousette and human cells exposed to double-stranded RNA and interferon (IFN). Bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, a pattern further supported by analysis of independent in vivo MARV infection datasets. In contrast, human cells activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation in response to MARV. Integrating transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, we identify species-specific immune programs encompassing differential IFN-stimulated gene regulation, apoptotic control, and cytokine signaling. Our findings establish an integrative framework for understanding species-specific antiviral responses associated with MARV reservoir biology, identify pathways linked to immunopathogenesis in humans, and provide a foundation for future studies of host responses to filovirus infection.

papers.abstract_en: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) has been implicated in immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, but herpesvirus-directed humoral responses across populations and disease states remain incompletely defined. We profiled antibodies to all nine human herpesviruses by PhIP-Seq in 908 serum samples from 848 individuals in Madagascar and Germany. Cohorts showed distinct reactivity patterns, including cross-virus associations between homologous alphaherpesvirus envelope glycoproteins. German cohorts recognized a broader range of latent and lytic EBV proteins than Malagasy controls, with increased reactivity in primary sclerosing cholangitis. Proteome-wide profiling detected reactivity to 60 of 79 EBV proteins; 29 contained at least one peptide recognized in >5% of participants. Co-occurrence analyses identified an EBNA2-EBNA3A/B/C module and BFRF3-EBNA1 and BZLF1-BMRF1 pairs in German cohorts. Peptide ELISA showed individual-level concordance with PhIP-Seq for EBNA1. These findings reveal geography- and disease-associated herpesvirus antibody repertoires incompletely captured by single-antigen serology.
